Front MatterPronunciation Key

Pronunciation Key

របៀបអានសូរសព្ទ

The Romanized Phonetics column is written for an English-speaking mouth — not for linguists. Read every syllable as written. Bold syllables carry the stress. Khmer has no tones, so keep your voice level and let the vowel length do the work.

Vowels

aas in but — short
aaas in father — long
ias in sit
ii / eeas in see
uas in put
ooas in food
eias in day
aeas in cat, stretched
aoas in now, shortened
oeas in her (no r)
uoglide oo → uh
ieglide ee → uh

Consonants to Watch

khpuffed k — never as in loch
phpuffed p — never f
thpuffed t — never as in the
ngas in singer — can begin a word
nyas in canyon
ra light tap, often softened
Golden Rule

Khmer final consonants are unreleased. In baat (បាទ) the mouth closes on the t but no air escapes — like the t in the British “that one”. Releasing it into “baa-tuh” is the single most common accent giveaway.

Greetings & Everyday Basics

Saying Hello & Goodbye

ការស្វាគមន៍ និងការលា

You walk into a small Phnom Penh coffee shop for the first time. The owner looks up from the counter.

Owner
ជម្រាបសួរ!
chom-RIEP suor!
Hello! (formal)
You
ជម្រាបសួរ បាទ។ សុខសប្បាយជាទេ?
chom-RIEP suor baat. sok sa-BAY chie tei?
Hello. How are you?
Owner
សុខសប្បាយ អរគុណ។ ចុះលោកវិញ?
sok sa-BAY, or-KUN. choh lowk vinh?
I’m well, thank you. And you?
You
ខ្ញុំក៏សុខសប្បាយដែរ។
khnyom kâ sok sa-BAY dae.
I’m fine too.
You (leaving)
អរគុណច្រើន។ ជួបគ្នាថ្ងៃក្រោយ!
or-KUN chraen. chuop knie thngai KRAOY!
Thank you. See you next time!
Say It Right

ជម្រាបសួរ is three syllables, not four: chom · riep · suor, with the weight on RIEP. The final r is barely there — closer to “sua” than “sewer”.

Ngorn Kakteka2Prepared by Nat Bunchhai

01

Saying Hello & Goodbye

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
Hello (formal, safe anywhere)ជម្រាបសួរchom-riep suor
Hi (casual, friends)សួស្តីsuor-sdei
Good morningអរុណសួស្តីa-run suor-sdei
Goodbye (everyday)លាហើយlie haoy
Goodbye (formal)ជម្រាបលាchom-riep lie
See you next timeជួបគ្នាថ្ងៃក្រោយchuop knie thngai kraoy
See you tomorrowជួបគ្នាថ្ងៃស្អែកchuop knie thngai sa-aek
Yes / polite “sir” (male speaker)បាទbaat
Yes / polite “ma’am” (female speaker)ចាសchaa
Thank youអរគុណor-kun
Pro-Tip · The Sampeah

Pair ជម្រាបសួរ with the sampeah — palms together at the chest, a small bow. The higher your hands, the more respect you show: chest for peers, mouth for elders and teachers, nose-bridge for monks and officials. A foreigner who returns a sampeah correctly is remembered warmly for it. And note the gender split: men end sentences with baat, women with chaa. Using the wrong one is the fastest way to get a friendly laugh.

Ngorn Kakteka3Prepared by Nat Bunchhai

02
Greetings & Everyday Basics

How Are You?

សុខទុក្ខ និងការសួរនាំ

You bump into a neighbour you haven’t seen in weeks — an exchange that is short, warm, and almost always ends with a question about food.

Neighbour
អូ! យូរហើយមិនបានជួបគ្នា។
ouh! YOO haoy min baan chuop knie.
Oh! Long time no see.
You
មែនហើយ! សុខសប្បាយជាទេ?
maen haoy! sok sa-BAY chie tei?
That’s right! How are you?
Neighbour
ធម្មតាទេ តែរវល់ណាស់។ ចុះបងវិញ?
thoam-ma-DAA tei, tae ro-VOL nas. choh bong vinh?
So-so, but very busy. And you?
Neighbour
ញ៉ាំបាយហើយនៅ?
nyam bai haoy nov?
Have you eaten yet?
You
ញ៉ាំហើយ បាទ។ អរគុណ។
NYAM haoy, baat. or-kun.
I’ve eaten already, thanks.
Say It Right

The question tag …ទេ? (tei?) turns almost any statement into a yes/no question, and it rises only slightly — Khmer does not swing the pitch the way English does. Over-lifting the end of sok sa-BAY chie tei? makes it sound anxious rather than friendly.

Ngorn Kakteka4Prepared by Nat Bunchhai

How Are You?

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
How are you?សុខសប្បាយជាទេ?sok sa-bay chie tei?
I’m fine, thank you.ខ្ញុំសុខសប្បាយ អរគុណ។khnyom sok sa-bay, or-kun
So-so / normal.ធម្មតាទេthoam-ma-daa tei

I’m very tired.ខ្ញុំនឿយហត់ណាស់khnyom nuey-hot nas
And you?ចុះអ្នកវិញ?choh neak vinh?

Yes, I’ve eaten already.ញ៉ាំហើយnyam haoy
Not yet.នៅទេnov tei

Pro-Tip · “Have You Eaten?”

ញ៉ាំបាយហើយនៅ? (nyam bai haoy nov?) is not really about food — it is Cambodia’s everyday “How’s it going?”, rooted in generations for whom a full stomach was the truest measure of well-being. Answer nyam haoy (“already eaten”) unless you actually want lunch — nov tei (“not yet”) is often taken as accepting an invitation you didn’t know you’d received.

Greetings & Everyday Basics

Introducing Yourself

ការណែនាំខ្លួន

A friend brings you to a family gathering, and everyone turns to look.

Sophea
តើអ្នកឈ្មោះអ្វី?
tae neak chhmuoh a-vei?
What is your name?
You
ខ្ញុំឈ្មោះ ដេវីត។ រីករាយដែលបានស្គាល់អ្នក។
khnyom chhmuoh David. rik-RIEY dael baan skoal neak.
My name is David. Nice to meet you.
Sophea
តើអ្នកមកពីប្រទេសណា?
tae neak mok pii bra-TEIH naa?
Which country are you from?
You
ខ្ញុំមកពីប្រទេសអង់គ្លេស។
khnyom mok pii bra-TEIH ong-GLEIH.
I’m from England.
Sophea
តើអ្នកធ្វើការអ្វី?
tae neak thveu KAA a-vei?
What work do you do?
You
ខ្ញុំជាគ្រូបង្រៀន។ សូមនិយាយយឺតៗ។
khnyom chie kruu bong-RIEN. som ni-yiey YOEUT-yoeut.
I’m a teacher. Please speak slowly.
Say It Right

ខ្ញុំ (khnyom, “I”) is one syllable — never “ker-nyom”. In fast speech it shortens to nyom, or drops out entirely.

Ngorn Kakteka6Prepared by Nat Bunchhai

My name is …ខ្ញុំឈ្មោះ …khnyom chhmuoh …
Nice to meet you.រីករាយដែលបានស្គាល់អ្នកrik-riey dael baan skoal neak

I’m from …ខ្ញុំមកពី …khnyom mok pii …
What work do you do?តើអ្នកធ្វើការអ្វី?tae neak thveu kaa a-vei?

Pro-Tip · Age Decides the Pronoun

Khmer has no neutral “you”. Before speaking, guess the person’s age relative to yours: bong (បង) for someone slightly older, p’oun (ប្អូន) for someone younger, lowk / lowk srei (លោក / លោកស្រី) for formal or senior, and om (ឪ​ម) for your parents’ generation. Calling an older person bong is always safe; calling them p’oun is not. Also expect your family name first — the author of this book, Ngorn Kakteka, is addressed as Kakteka.

Greetings & Everyday Basics

Asking Someone’s Name

ការសួរឈ្មោះ

You have met this person twice now and still cannot remember what to call them. Ask — nobody minds.

You
សូមទោស ខ្ញុំភ្លេចឈ្មោះអ្នក។
som TOH, khnyom phlech chhmuoh neak.
Sorry, I’ve forgotten your name.
Dara
អត់អីទេ។ ខ្ញុំឈ្មោះ សុខ ដារា។
ot ei TEI. khnyom chhmuoh Sok Dara.
No problem. My name is Sok Dara.
You
តើខ្ញុំគួរហៅអ្នកយ៉ាងម៉េច?
tae khnyom kuor hav neak yang MECH?
What should I call you?
Dara
ហៅខ្ញុំថា បងដារា បានហើយ។
hav khnyom thaa BONG Dara baan haoy.
Just call me Bong Dara.
You
តើសរសេរយ៉ាងម៉េច?
tae sor-SEI yang mech?
How do you write it?
Say It Right

ភ្លេច (phlech) starts with a puffed p, not an f. English speakers reach for “flech” — the mouth position is closer to “p-lech” said quickly.

Ngorn Kakteka8Prepared by Nat Bunchhai

Asking Someone’s Name

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
What should I call you?តើខ្ញុំគួរហៅអ្នកយ៉ាងម៉េច?tae khnyom kuor hav neak yang mech?

My nickname is …ឈ្មោះហៅក្រៅខ្ញុំគឺ …chhmuoh hav krav khnyom keu …
Sorry, I forgot your name.សូមទោស ខ្ញុំភ្លេចឈ្មោះអ្នកsom toh, khnyom phlech chhmuoh neak

How do you write it?តើសរសេរយ៉ាងម៉េច?tae sor-sei yang mech?
No problem.អត់អីទេot ei tei

Pro-Tip · Everyone Has Two Names

The name on the ID card is often not the name anyone uses. Most Cambodians go by a one-syllable nickname given in childhood — Ti, Srey, Bong, Nak — and colleagues of twenty years may never learn the formal one. Ask for the ឈ្មោះហៅក្រៅ (chhmuoh hav krav) and use it. Attach bong or p’oun in front and you sound like a local, not a form.

Ngorn Kakteka9Prepared by Nat Bunchhai
Chapter 1 · Greetings & Everyday BasicsSituation 05
05
Greetings & Everyday Basics

Please, Thank You & Sorry

សូម អរគុណ និងសូមទោស

Three words carry more goodwill than any amount of vocabulary. Here they are in one exchange.

You
សូមទោស! ជួយខ្ញុំបន្តិចផង។
som TOH! chuoy khnyom bon-tech phong.
Excuse me! Please help me a moment.
Woman
បាទ មានរឿងអ្វី?
baat, mien ROEUNG a-vei?
Yes, what’s the matter?
You
សូមប្រាប់ផ្លូវទៅផ្សារ។
som BRAB phlov teuv phsaa.
Please tell me the way to the market.
You
អរគុណច្រើន!
or-KUN chraen!
Thank you very much!
Woman
មិនអីទេ។ អញ្ជើញ។
min ei TEI. an-choeun.
It’s nothing. Go ahead.
Say It Right

សូម (som) rhymes with English “some” and goes in front of the verb, never at the end: som brab, not “brab som”.

Ngorn Kakteka10Prepared by Nat Bunchhai
Chapter 1 · Greetings & Everyday BasicsSituation 05
05

Please, Thank You & Sorry

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
Please … (before a verb)សូម …som …
Thank youអរគុណor-kun
Thank you very muchអរគុណច្រើនor-kun chraen
Sorry / excuse meសូមទោសsom toh
It’s nothing / never mindមិនអីទេmin ei tei
Please help me.ជួយខ្ញុំផងchuoy khnyom phong
No need, thank you.មិនបាច់ទេ អរគុណmin bach tei, or-kun
Please, go ahead. (inviting)អញ្ជើញan-choeun
Pro-Tip · There Is No “You’re Welcome”

Khmer has no single reply to thanks. Cambodians answer with អត់អីទេ (ot ei tei) or មិនអីទេ (min ei tei) — both meaning “it’s nothing”. And សូមទោស does double duty: it is your apology and your “excuse me” for squeezing past someone in a crowded market. Say it with a small dip of the head and it never sounds abrupt.

Ngorn Kakteka11Prepared by Nat Bunchhai

Greetings & Everyday Basics

Yes, No & “I Don’t Understand”

បាទ ទេ និងខ្ញុំមិនយល់

Someone is speaking to you at full speed. These five sentences buy you time without ending the conversation.

Man
តើអ្នកយល់ទេ?
tae neak YUL tei?
Do you understand?
You
អត់ទេ ខ្ញុំមិនយល់ទេ។
ot TEI, khnyom min YUL tei.
No, I don’t understand.
You
តើវាមានន័យថាម៉េច?
tae vie mien NEY thaa mech?
What does it mean?
Man
មានន័យថា «ថ្ងៃស្អែក»។
mien NEY thaa “thngai sa-aek”.
It means “tomorrow”.
You
អា! ខ្ញុំយល់ហើយ។ អរគុណ។
aa! khnyom YUL haoy. or-kun.
Ah! Now I understand. Thanks.
Say It Right

The negative is a sandwich: min … tei wraps around the verb. ខ្ញុំមិនយល់ទេ is literally “I not understand no”. Drop the final tei and it sounds unfinished.

Ngorn Kakteka12Prepared by Nat Bunchhai
Chapter 1 · Greetings & Everyday BasicsSituation 06
06

Yes, No & “I Don’t Understand”

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
Yes (male / female)បាទ / ចាសbaat / chaa
No / notទេ / អត់ទេtei / ot tei
I understand.ខ្ញុំយល់ហើយkhnyom yul haoy
I don’t understand.ខ្ញុំមិនយល់ទេkhnyom min yul tei
What does it mean?មានន័យថាម៉េច?mien ney thaa mech?
I don’t know.ខ្ញុំមិនដឹងទេkhnyom min deung tei
That’s not right.មិនមែនទេmin maen tei
Correct / that’s right.ត្រូវហើយtrov haoy
Pro-Tip · “Yes” Often Means “I’m Listening”

A Cambodian nodding baat, baat, baat through your explanation is telling you they can hear you — not that they agree, and not that they understood. Direct refusal is felt as harsh, so a genuine “no” usually arrives dressed as “maybe”, “a bit difficult”, or a smile and silence. When something matters, ask the person to tell you the plan back in their own words.

Ngorn Kakteka13Prepared by Nat Bunchhai

07
Greetings & Everyday Basics

Repeat & Speak Slowly

សូមនិយាយម្ដងទៀត

The most valuable page in this book. Learn these before anything else — they keep every other conversation alive.

Seller
មួយគីឡូបីពាន់រៀល។
muoy ki-LOU bei poan riel.
Three thousand riel a kilo.
You
សូមទោស សូមនិយាយយឺតៗ។
som toh, som ni-yiey YOEUT-yoeut.
Sorry, please speak slowly.
Seller
បី... ពាន់... រៀល។
bei … POAN … riel.
Three … thousand … riel.
You
សូមសរសេរឲ្យខ្ញុំផង។
som sor-sei AOY khnyom phong.
Please write it for me.
You
ឥឡូវខ្ញុំយល់ហើយ។ អរគុណ។
eu-LOV khnyom yul haoy. or-kun.
Now I understand. Thank you.
Say It Right

Doubling a word softens or stretches it. យឺតៗ (yoeut-yoeut) is “slowly, slowly”; the little mark ៗ means “say it twice”. You will see it everywhere.

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
Please speak slowly.សូមនិយាយយឺតៗsom ni-yiey yoeut-yoeut
Please say it again.សូមនិយាយម្ដងទៀតsom ni-yiey mdong tiet
Please speak louder.សូមនិយាយឮៗsom ni-yiey lu-lu

Please write it for me.សូមសរសេរឲ្យខ្ញុំផងsom sor-sei aoy khnyom phong
How do you say … in Khmer?… ជាភាសាខ្មែរនិយាយយ៉ាងម៉េច?… chie phie-saa khmae ni-yiey yang mech?

Pro-Tip · Ask for the Pen

Cambodian numbers are the hardest thing on this page to hear at speed, and every price in the country is negotiable in writing. Carrying a small notebook — or handing over your phone’s calculator — turns a failed exchange into a friendly one in two seconds. Sellers do this with each other constantly; it is not a foreigner’s crutch, it is normal practice.

Greetings & Everyday Basics

Where Are You From?

តើអ្នកមកពីណា?

Within thirty seconds of meeting you, someone will ask this. Have the whole answer ready.

Driver
តើអ្នកមកពីប្រទេសណា?
tae neak mok pii bra-TEIH naa?
Which country are you from?
You
ខ្ញុំមកពីប្រទេសអូស្ត្រាលី។
khnyom mok pii bra-TEIH ou-straa-lii.
I’m from Australia.
Driver
តើអ្នកនៅកម្ពុជាបានប៉ុន្មានហើយ?
tae neak nov kam-pu-chie baan PON-man haoy?
How long have you been in Cambodia?
You
បានពីរឆ្នាំហើយ។
baan PII chhnam haoy.
Two years now.
You
ខ្ញុំចូលចិត្តកម្ពុជាណាស់។
khnyom chol-CHET kam-pu-chie nas.
I like Cambodia very much.
Say It Right

The country’s own name is កម្ពុជា (kam-pu-chie) — four beats, stress light throughout. “Cambodia” is the English exonym; using the Khmer one always earns a smile.

Phrases

Key Phrases

America / Englandអាមេរិក / អង់គ្លេសaa-mei-rik / ong-gleih
France / Australiaបារាំង / អូស្ត្រាលីbaa-rang / ou-straa-lii
Japan / Chinaជប៉ុន / ចិនchie-pon / chen
How long have you been here?តើអ្នកនៅទីនេះបានប៉ុន្មានហើយ?tae neak nov ti-nih baan pon-man haoy?
It’s my first time.ជាលើកទីមួយchie leuk ti muoy
I like Cambodia very much.ខ្ញុំចូលចិត្តកម្ពុជាណាស់khnyom chol-chet kam-pu-chie nas

Pro-Tip · The Questions That Follow

Expect the next three questions to be your age, marital status and salary — in that order, from someone you met four minutes ago. This is not nosiness. Age settles which pronoun to use, and the rest is ordinary friendly accounting. A vague answer is perfectly acceptable: ចាំមួយភ្លែត (cham muoy phlet — “hang on a second”) and a laugh closes the subject with no offence taken.

Greetings & Everyday Basics

Talking About the Weather

និយាយអំពីអាកាសធាតុ

Cambodia has two seasons and one universal complaint. Both are excellent conversation starters.

Neighbour
ថ្ងៃនេះក្ដៅណាស់!
thngai nih KDAV nas!
It’s so hot today!
You
មែនហើយ ក្ដៅពេក។
maen haoy, KDAV peik.
Yes, too hot.
Neighbour
ល្ងាចនេះប្រហែលភ្លៀងធ្លាក់។
lngiech nih bra-HAEL pleang thleak.
It will probably rain this evening.
You
រដូវវស្សាមកដល់ហើយ។
ro-DOV voa-saa mok dol haoy.
The rainy season has arrived.
You
ខ្ញុំចូលចិត្តរដូវត្រជាក់ជាង។
khnyom chol-chet ro-dov tro-CHEAK chieng.
I prefer the cool season.
Say It Right

ក្ដៅ (kdav) is one syllable — the k and d are pressed together with no vowel between them. Khmer is full of these clusters; resist the urge to insert “kuh-dav”.

Talking About the Weather

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
It’s very hot.ក្ដៅណាស់kdav nas
It’s cool / cold.ត្រជាក់tro-cheak
It’s raining.ភ្លៀងធ្លាក់pleang thleak
It’s very windy.ខ្យល់បក់ខ្លាំងkhyol bok khlang
The rainy seasonរដូវវស្សាro-dov voa-saa
The dry seasonរដូវប្រាំងro-dov prang

Pro-Tip · Complaining Is Bonding

Grumbling about the heat is a social ritual, not a conversation about meteorology. A well-timed ក្ដៅណាស់! to a stranger waiting out a downpour with you will get a laugh and often a chair. Note also that Cambodians divide the year into hot, rainy and a brief, treasured cool season around December — mention preferring the cool one and you will get instant agreement.

Greetings & Everyday Basics

Numbers & Telling Time

លេខ និងម៉ោង

Numbers unlock prices, addresses and appointments. Learn one to ten today; the rest is arithmetic.

You
ឥឡូវម៉ោងប៉ុន្មានហើយ?
eu-lov MAONG pon-man haoy?
What time is it now?
Friend
ម៉ោងបួនកន្លះរសៀល។
MAONG buon kon-lah ro-siel.
Half past four in the afternoon.
You
តើយើងជួបគ្នាម៉ោងប៉ុន្មាន?
tae yeung chuop knie MAONG pon-man?
What time shall we meet?
Friend
ម៉ោងប្រាំពីរល្ងាច បានទេ?
maong PRAM-pil lngiech, baan tei?
Seven in the evening, alright?
You
បាទ បានហើយ។ ជួបគ្នាថ្ងៃស្អែក។
baat, BAAN haoy. chuop knie thngai sa-aek.
Yes, that works. See you tomorrow.
Say It Right

Khmer counts to five, then adds: six is pram-muoy (5+1), seven pram-pil (5+2), up to nine. Hear pram- and you already know the number is between six and nine.

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics

Pro-Tip · Read the Price Tags

Khmer has its own numerals — ១ ២ ៣ ៤ ៥ ៦ ៧ ៨ ៩ ០ — and they appear on market price tags, bus tickets, house numbers and government forms, often instead of Western digits. Ten minutes spent memorising the shapes will save you a hundred confused transactions. Note that ៥ (5) and ៨ (8) are the two most commonly misread by beginners.

Getting Around

Hailing a Tuk-Tuk

ការហៅតុកតុក

A driver calls out to you from the kerb. Answering in Khmer changes the price before you have even sat down.

Driver
តុកតុកទេ លោក? ទៅណា?
tuk-tuk tei, lowk? teuv NAA?
Tuk-tuk, sir? Where to?
You
ទៅផ្សារធំថ្មី បានទេ?
teuv phsaa thom THMEI, baan tei?
To the Central Market, is that okay?
Driver
បាទ បាន។ អញ្ជើញឡើង។
baat, BAAN. an-choeun laeung.
Yes, fine. Please get in.
You
ចាំបន្តិច តម្លៃប៉ុន្មាន?
cham bon-tech, tom-LAI pon-man?
Hold on — how much is it?
Driver
បីដុល្លារ បាទ។
bei dol-LAA, baat.
Three dollars.
Say It Right

Settle the price before you climb in — cham bon-tech (“hold on a second”) is the phrase that buys you that moment, and every Cambodian passenger uses it.

Ngorn Kakteka23Prepared by Nat Bunchhai
Chapter 2 · Getting AroundSituation 11
11

Hailing a Tuk-Tuk

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
Where are you going?ទៅណា?teuv naa?
I want to go to …ខ្ញុំចង់ទៅ …khnyom chong teuv …
Can you take me to …?ទៅ … បានទេ?teuv … baan tei?
How much is it?តម្លៃប៉ុន្មាន?tom-lai pon-man?
Hold on a second.ចាំបន្តិចcham bon-tech
Motorbike taxiម៉ូតូឌុបmoto-dup
Are you free? (available)ទំនេរទេ?tum-nei tei?
No thanks, I’ll walk.អត់ទេ ខ្ញុំដើរot tei, khnyom daeu
Pro-Tip · Tuk-Tuk, Remork, Moto

What tourists call a tuk-tuk, Cambodians usually call a រ៉ឺម៉ក (rermok) — a carriage towed behind a motorbike. The small Indian-style auto-rickshaws that arrived with the ride apps are the true tuk-tuk, and they are cheaper. A moto-dup — you riding pillion on a motorbike — is cheapest and fastest of all, and is how most of Phnom Penh actually moves.

Chapter 2 · Getting AroundSituation 12

Getting Around

Negotiating the Fare

ការតថ្លៃឡាន

The first price is an opening offer, not an insult. Smile, halve it, and meet in the middle.

Driver
ប្រាំដុល្លារ។
PRAM dol-laa.
Five dollars.
You
ថ្លៃពេក! បញ្ចុះតម្លៃបានទេ?
THLAI peik! banh-choh tom-lai baan tei?
Too expensive! Can you lower it?
You
បីដុល្លារ បានទេ?
bei dol-LAA, baan tei?
Three dollars, alright?
Driver
បួនដុល្លារ ចុងក្រោយ។
buon dol-laa, chong-KRAOY.
Four dollars, final.
You
អញ្ចឹងបានហើយ។ ទៅ!
an-CHOENG baan haoy. teuv!
Alright then. Let’s go!
Say It Right

ថ្លៃ (thlai) means expensive; តម្លៃ (tom-lai) means price. One syllable apart, and mixing them up is the most common bargaining slip.

Ngorn Kakteka25Prepared by Nat Bunchhai

Negotiating the Fare

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
Too expensive!ថ្លៃពេក!thlai peik!
Can you lower the price?បញ្ចុះតម្លៃបានទេ?banh-choh tom-lai baan tei?

Return trip tooទៅមកវិញផងteuv mok vinh phong
I’ll pay when we arrive.ដល់ហើយទើបបង់លុយdol haoy teub bong luy
Pro-Tip · The Round-Trip Discount

The strongest card you hold is not haggling — it is volume. Asking a driver to wait and bring you back (teuv mok vinh phong) often costs barely more than the one-way fare, because he keeps the fare instead of hunting a new passenger. Do this twice with the same driver and you have a regular: save his number, and you will never negotiate again.

Getting Around

Directing the Driver

ការប្រាប់ផ្លូវអ្នកបើកបរ

Cambodian addresses are unreliable; landmarks are everything. Six words of direction will get you home.

You
សូមទៅត្រង់។
som teuv TRONG.
Please go straight.
You
បត់ឆ្វេងនៅចំណុចនោះ។
bot CHVENG nov chom-noch nuh.
Turn left at that corner.
Driver
ក្រោយវត្តមែនទេ?
kraoy VOAT maen tei?
Behind the pagoda, right?
You
បាទ ត្រូវហើយ។ បន្តិចទៀត។
baat, TROV haoy. bon-tech tiet.
Yes, correct. A little further.
You
ឈប់ទីនេះ! ដល់ហើយ។
CHHUP ti-nih! dol haoy.
Stop here! We’ve arrived.
Say It Right

ឆ្វេង (chveng, left) and ស្ដាំ (sdam, right) are worth over-learning. Point with your whole hand as you say them — pointing with one finger is impolite here.

Ngorn Kakteka27Prepared by Nat Bunchhai
Chapter 2 · Getting AroundSituation 13
13

Directing the Driver

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
Go straight.ទៅត្រង់teuv trong
Turn left / turn rightបត់ឆ្វេង / បត់ស្ដាំbot chveng / bot sdam
Stop here!ឈប់ទីនេះ!chhup ti-nih!

Behind the pagodaក្រោយវត្តkraoy voat
We’ve arrived.ដល់ហើយdol haoy
Pro-Tip · Navigate by Landmark

Street numbers exist in Phnom Penh but almost nobody navigates by them, and outside the capital they barely exist at all. Cambodians steer by landmarks: វត្ត (voat, pagoda), ផ្សារ (phsaa, market), a petrol station, a well-known hotel. Learn the three landmarks nearest your home and you will never be lost again — “behind the pagoda” beats any address.

Getting Around

Using a Ride App

ការប្រើកម្មវិធីហៅឡាន

The app has set the price, but the driver still calls you. Here is that thirty-second phone conversation.

Driver
ហាឡូ! លោកនៅឯណា?
haa-LOU! lowk nov ae-naa?
Hello! Where are you?
You
ខ្ញុំនៅមុខសណ្ឋាគារ។
khnyom nov MUK son-thaa-kie.
I’m in front of the hotel.
Driver
ចាំបួនប្រាំនាទី។
cham buon pram NIE-ti.
Wait four or five minutes.
You
បាទ។ ខ្ញុំពាក់អាវក្រហម។
baat. khnyom peak aav KRO-HOM.
Okay. I’m wearing a red shirt.
You
ខ្ញុំបង់តាមកម្មវិធី។
khnyom bong taam kam-ma-vi-THII.
I’m paying through the app.
Say It Right

On the phone, lead with where you are standing, not your name. khnyom nov muk … (“I’m in front of …”) is the single most useful sentence in this whole situation.

Ngorn Kakteka29Prepared by Nat Bunchhai

Using a Ride App

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics

Pro-Tip · The App Price Is the Real Price

Apps such as PassApp, Grab and TADA fix the fare in advance, which quietly ends the whole negotiation game — and they are usually cheaper than a street tuk-tuk for a foreigner. Keep your phone in Khmer-friendly mode: drivers will phone rather than message, and they will speak fast. The four phrases above cover ninety per cent of those calls.

Getting Around

Renting a Motorbike

ការជួលម៉ូតូ

Renting is easy; the paperwork and the fuel are where foreigners get caught. Ask all four questions.

You
ខ្ញុំចង់ជួលម៉ូតូមួយ។
khnyom chong CHUOL moto muoy.
I’d like to rent a motorbike.
Owner
មួយថ្ងៃប្រាំដុល្លារ។
muoy thngai PRAM dol-laa.
Five dollars a day.
You
មួយខែថ្លៃប៉ុន្មាន?
muoy KHAE thlai pon-man?
How much for a month?
You
មានមួកសុវត្ថិភាពទេ?
mien muok so-vat-thi-PHIEP tei?
Is there a helmet?
Owner
មាន។ សូមទុកលិខិតឆ្លងដែន។
MIEN. som tuk li-khet chhlong-daen.
Yes. Please leave your passport.
Say It Right

ជួល (chuol) covers both rent and hire. Say chuol muoy khae — “rent one month” — and the daily rate usually drops by half.

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics

Pro-Tip · Never Leave Your Passport

Many rental shops ask for your passport as security. Offer a photocopy plus a deposit instead — reputable shops accept this, and recovering a held passport during a dispute is genuinely difficult. Photograph the bike from all four sides before you ride off, scratches included, and check that the shop provides a helmet: police fine riders without one, and foreigners are stopped far more often.

Getting Around

At the Bus Station

នៅស្ថានីយ៍ឡាន

Buying an intercity ticket. Know the departure time, the seat and whether it stops where you think.

You
សុំសំបុត្រទៅសៀមរាបមួយ។
som SOM-BOT teuv siem-riep muoy.
One ticket to Siem Reap, please.
Clerk
ចេញម៉ោងប្រាំបីព្រឹក។
chenh maong PRAM-bei pruk.
It leaves at eight in the morning.
You
ធ្វើដំណើរប៉ុន្មានម៉ោង?
thveu dom-NAEU pon-man maong?
How many hours is the journey?
Clerk
ប្រាំមួយម៉ោង។ ដប់ពីរដុល្លារ។
PRAM-muoy maong. dop-pii dol-laa.
Six hours. Twelve dollars.
You
សុំកៅអីជាប់បង្អួច។
som kav-ei CHOAB bong-uoch.
A window seat, please.
Say It Right

ចេញ (chenh) means to leave / depart and ដល់ (dol) means to arrive. Two words that answer nearly every travel question you will ever ask.

Ngorn Kakteka33Prepared by Nat Bunchhai
Chapter 2 · Getting AroundSituation 16
16

At the Bus Station

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
One ticket to …សុំសំបុត្រទៅ … មួយsom som-bot teuv … muoy
What time does it leave?ចេញម៉ោងប៉ុន្មាន?chenh maong pon-man?
What time does it arrive?ដល់ម៉ោងប៉ុន្មាន?dol maong pon-man?
How many hours?ប៉ុន្មានម៉ោង?pon-man maong?
A window seat, please.សុំកៅអីជាប់បង្អួចsom kav-ei choab bong-uoch
Is it air-conditioned?មានម៉ាស៊ីនត្រជាក់ទេ?mien maa-sin tro-cheak tei?
Which platform / where?ចេញនៅឯណា?chenh nov ae-naa?
Round tripទៅមកវិញteuv mok vinh
Pro-Tip · Buy the Day Before

Popular routes — Phnom Penh to Siem Reap, Sihanoukville, Battambang — sell out on weekends and vanish entirely around Khmer New Year and Pchum Ben, when the whole country travels home at once. Buy a day ahead, arrive thirty minutes early, and keep your ticket visible: seats are assigned but rarely enforced, and the polite passenger who shows up last stands.

Getting Around

On a Long-Distance Bus

នៅលើឡានក្រុង

Six hours, one rest stop, and a seat that may already have someone in it. Sort it out politely.

You
សូមទោស នេះកៅអីខ្ញុំ។
som toh, nih KAV-EI khnyom.
Excuse me, this is my seat.
Passenger
អូ សូមទោស! ខ្ញុំប្ដូរ។
ouh, som TOH! khnyom bdo.
Oh, sorry! I’ll move.
You
តើឈប់សម្រាកនៅឯណា?
tae chhup som-RAAK nov ae-naa?
Where do we stop for a break?
Driver
ឈប់កម្ពង់ធំ សាមសិបនាទី។
chhup kom-pong-THOM, saam-sep nie-ti.
We stop at Kampong Thom, thirty minutes.
You
សូមប្រាប់ខ្ញុំពេលដល់។
som BRAB khnyom peil dol.
Please tell me when we arrive.
Say It Right

សូមប្រាប់ខ្ញុំពេលដល់ (som brab khnyom peil dol) — “tell me when we arrive” — is worth memorising whole. Say it to the driver’s assistant, not the driver, and you will be woken at the right town.

Pro-Tip · The Assistant Runs the Bus

Every intercity bus has a young assistant who loads luggage, collects tickets and shouts the stops. He is the person to ask, not the driver. Learn his job title — ជំនួយការ (chum-nuoy-kaa) — or simply catch his eye with bong. Tell him your destination when you board and he will make sure you are off the bus at the right place.

Ferries & Boats

ទូក និងសាឡាង

Crossing the Mekong, or heading out to an island. Ask about the life jackets — politely, but ask.

You
ទូកចេញម៉ោងប៉ុន្មាន?
TOUK chenh maong pon-man?
What time does the boat leave?
Boatman
ម៉ោងប្រាំបួនកន្លះ។
maong PRAM-buon kon-lah.
Half past nine.
You
ជិះប៉ុន្មានម៉ោងទៅកោះ?
CHIH pon-man maong teuv koh?
How many hours to the island?
Boatman
មួយម៉ោងកន្លះ។
muoy maong KON-LAH.
An hour and a half.
You
មានអាវសង្គ្រោះទេ?
mien aav song-KROH tei?
Are there life jackets?

ជិះ (chih) is the verb for riding anything you sit on — boat, bus, bike, horse, elephant. chih touk, chih moto, chih laan.

Ferries & Boats

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
Boatទូកtouk
Islandកោះkoh
River / seaទន្លេ / សមុទ្រton-lei / sa-mot
What time does the boat leave?ទូកចេញម៉ោងប៉ុន្មាន?touk chenh maong pon-man?
Are there life jackets?មានអាវសង្គ្រោះទេ?mien aav song-kroh tei?

Pro-Tip · Ask About the Last Boat First

Island and river services run to the weather and the number of passengers, not to the timetable painted on the jetty. Before you board anything, ask touk chong-kraoy tro-lop maong pon-man? — “what time is the last boat back?” — and then take the one before it. In the rainy season a cancelled afternoon crossing can strand you overnight, and the guesthouses know it.

Airport & Immigration

ព្រលានយន្តហោះ និងអន្តោប្រវេសន៍

Immigration is conducted in English, but a Khmer greeting at the counter costs nothing and often shortens things.

Officer
សូមលិខិតឆ្លងដែន។
som li-khet CHHLONG-daen.
Passport, please.
You
នេះបាទ។ ជម្រាបសួរ។
nih BAAT. chom-riep suor.
Here you are. Hello.
Officer
មកធ្វើអ្វី? ស្នាក់នៅប៉ុន្មានថ្ងៃ?
mok THVEU a-vei? snak-nov pon-man thngai?
Why are you here? How many days?
You
មកទេសចរណ៍ ដប់បួនថ្ងៃ។
mok teih-sa-CHOA, dop-buon thngai.
Tourism, fourteen days.
You
ខ្ញុំស្នាក់នៅសណ្ឋាគារភ្នំពេញ។
khnyom SNAK-nov son-thaa-kie phnom-penh.
I’m staying at a hotel in Phnom Penh.
Say It Right

ស្នាក់នៅ (snak-nov) means to stay / lodge, as opposed to រស់នៅ (ruoh-nov), to live. Officials care a great deal about which one you say.

Airport & Immigration

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics

Visaទិដ្ឋាការtet-thaa-kaa

Pro-Tip · Have the Exact Fee Ready

Visa-on-arrival is paid in US dollars, in cash, and the counter rarely gives change gracefully. Bring the exact amount plus a passport photo, and keep small notes separate from large ones. If anyone at the airport asks for an extra “processing fee” beyond the posted price, a calm som toh, khnyom min yul tei — “sorry, I don’t understand” — with a smile is remarkably effective.

Getting Around

Asking for Directions

ការសួរផ្លូវ

Lost on foot. Ask a shopkeeper rather than a passer-by — they know the street and they are not in a hurry.

You
សូមទោស ផ្សារនៅឯណា?
som toh, PHSAA nov ae-naa?
Excuse me, where is the market?
Shopkeeper
ទៅត្រង់ រួចបត់ស្ដាំ។
teuv TRONG, ruoch bot sdam.
Go straight, then turn right.
You
ឆ្ងាយទេ? ដើរបានទេ?
CHHNGAY tei? daeu baan tei?
Is it far? Can I walk?
Shopkeeper
ជិតណាស់ ដប់នាទី។
CHIT nas, dop nie-ti.
Very close, ten minutes.
You
អរគុណច្រើន បង!
or-KUN chraen, bong!
Thank you very much!
Say It Right

Open with សូមទោស (som toh) every single time. Walking up and launching straight into a question reads as abrupt, even when your Khmer is otherwise perfect.

Asking for Directions

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics

Is it far?ឆ្ងាយទេ?chhngay tei?

Toilet / bank / post officeបង្គន់ / ធនាគារ / ប្រៃសណីយ៍bong-kon / thie-nie-kie / prai-sa-nii

Pro-Tip · Nobody Will Tell You They Don’t Know

Saying “I don’t know” to a guest feels unhelpful, so a person who is unsure will often point anyway — confidently, and sometimes wrongly. The fix is simple: ask two people, a hundred metres apart, and go with the answer they agree on. Better still, show the place on your phone map; a picture removes the pressure to guess entirely.

Food & Drink

Getting a Table

ការរកតុអង្គុយ

You walk into a busy local restaurant. Nobody comes to seat you — you announce yourself instead.

You
សូមទោស មានតុទំនេរទេ?
som toh, mien TOK tum-nei tei?
Excuse me, is there a free table?
Waiter
មាន បាទ។ ប៉ុន្មាននាក់?
MIEN, baat. pon-man neak?
Yes. How many people?
You
ពីរនាក់ បាទ។
PII neak, baat.
Two people.
You
សុំតុនៅខាងក្រៅបានទេ?
som tok nov khang-KRAV baan tei?
Could we sit outside?
Waiter
អញ្ជើញ។ នេះម៉ឺនុយ។
an-CHOEUN. nih meu-nuy.
Please. Here’s the menu.
Say It Right

People are counted with នាក់ (neak): pii neak, bei neak. Say the number first, then the counter — never the other way round.

Ngorn Kakteka44Prepared by Nat Bunchhai
Chapter 3 · Food & DrinkSituation 21

Getting a Table

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
Is there a free table?មានតុទំនេរទេ?mien tok tum-nei tei?

Menuម៉ឺនុយmeu-nuy

Pro-Tip · Nobody Seats You

In most Cambodian restaurants there is no host at the door. You walk in, find a table and sit down; staff arrive once you are settled. To call a waiter, raise a hand and say bong! — it is normal, not rude. What is rude is clicking your fingers or calling out “hey”. And the plastic-stool place with no menu is often the best food on the street.

Food & Drink

Ordering Food

ការកុម្ម៉ង់ម្ហូប

One word — som — plus the name of a dish is a complete, polite order. Everything else is decoration.

Waiter
ញ៉ាំអ្វីដែរ បង?
NYAM a-vei dae, bong?
What will you have?
You
សុំបាយឆាសាច់មាន់មួយ។
som bay-CHHAA sach moan muoy.
One chicken fried rice, please.
You
មានអាម៉ុកទេ?
mien AA-MOK tei?
Do you have amok?
Waiter
មាន បាទ។ ត្រី ឬសាច់មាន់?
MIEN, baat. trei reu sach moan?
Yes. Fish or chicken?
You
ត្រី បាទ។ អស់ប៉ុណ្ណោះ។
TREI, baat. oh pon-noh.
Fish. That’s all.
Say It Right

Quantity goes last: som bay-chhaa muoy is “please, fried rice, one”. Front-loading the number the English way — “one fried rice” — is understood, but marks you instantly.

Ordering Food

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
I’d like … (one)សុំ … មួយsom … muoy
Do you have …?មាន … ទេ?mien … tei?
Rice / fried riceបាយ / បាយឆាbay / bay-chhaa
Noodle soupគុយទាវkuy-tiev
Chicken / pork / beefសាច់មាន់ / សាច់ជ្រូក / សាច់គោsach moan / sach chruk / sach kou
Fish / prawn / vegetablesត្រី / បង្គា / បន្លែtrei / bong-kie / bon-lae
What do you recommend?មុខណាឆ្ងាញ់?muk naa chhngañ?
That’s all, thank you.អស់ប៉ុណ្ណោះ អរគុណoh pon-noh, or-kun
Pro-Tip · Order the Way Cambodians Do

A Khmer meal is shared: two or three dishes land in the middle with a communal bowl of rice, and everybody takes small amounts onto their own plate. Ordering one dish each, Western style, produces a strange table. Ask muk naa chhngañ? — “which dish is delicious?” — and let the waiter build the meal. You will eat better and spend less.

Food & Drink

Drinks & Coffee

ភេសជ្ជៈ និងកាហ្វេ

Khmer iced coffee is sweet, strong and served with condensed milk unless you say otherwise. Say otherwise early.

You
សុំកាហ្វេទឹកកកមួយ។
som kaa-fei TUK-KOK muoy.
One iced coffee, please.
Seller
ដាក់ទឹកដោះគោទេ?
dak tuk-doh-KOU tei?
With milk?
You
អត់ទេ ហើយកុំដាក់ស្ករច្រើន។
ot tei, haoy kom dak SKO chraen.
No, and not much sugar.
You
សុំទឹកសុទ្ធមួយដបទៀត។
som tuk SOT muoy dop tiet.
And one bottle of water.
Seller
បាទ ចាំបន្តិច។
baat, CHAM bon-tech.
Yes, one moment.
Say It Right

កុំ (kom) is “don’t” and goes before the verb: kom dak sko — “don’t put sugar”. It is direct without being rude, which is exactly what you want when ordering.

Ngorn Kakteka48Prepared by Nat Bunchhai

Drinks & Coffee

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
Water / bottled waterទឹក / ទឹកសុទ្ធtuk / tuk sot

Coffee / teaកាហ្វេ / តែkaa-fei / tae
Iced coffee with milkកាហ្វេទឹកដោះគោទឹកកកkaa-fei tuk-doh-kou tuk-kok

Pro-Tip · Sweet Is the Default

Cambodian coffee arrives with a thick layer of condensed milk at the bottom and sugar on top of that. If you want it plain, say so before the glass is built — afterwards nothing can be done. Ask for កាហ្វេខ្មៅ (kaa-fei khmav), “black coffee”, and add kom dak sko. Ice in reputable shops is factory-made and safe; the cylindrical kind with a hole through the middle is the one to trust.

Food & Drink

“Not Spicy, Please”

សុំកុំឲ្យហឹរ

Khmer food is milder than Thai, but the chilli dish on the table is not. Set your limits at the point of order.

You
សុំកុំឲ្យហឹរ បាទ។
som kom aoy HOEU, baat.
Not spicy, please.
Waiter
មិនហឹរសោះ ឬហឹរបន្តិច?
min hoeu SOH reu hoeu bon-tech?
Not at all, or a little spicy?
You
ហឹរបន្តិចបាន។
hoeu BON-TECH baan.
A little is fine.
You
ខ្ញុំមិនញ៉ាំម្ទេសទេ។
khnyom min nyam MTEIH tei.
I don’t eat chilli.
Waiter
បាទ យល់ហើយ។
baat, YUL haoy.
Yes, understood.
Say It Right

ហឹរ (hoeu) is spicy-hot; ក្ដៅ (kdav) is hot in temperature. Asking for food that is not kdav will get you a cold plate.

“Not Spicy, Please”

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
Not spicy, please.សុំកុំឲ្យហឹរsom kom aoy hoeu

Pro-Tip · Season at the Table

Khmer cooking is built to be adjusted by the eater, which is why every table carries chilli, fish sauce, sugar, lime and pepper. Ordering mild and then seasoning your own bowl is completely normal and slightly insults nobody. The famous exception is ទឹកត្រី (tuk-trei, fermented fish sauce) — it is already inside almost every dish, so a genuine fish allergy needs stating clearly and early.

Food & Drink

Street Food Stalls

ម្ហូបតាមចិញ្ចើមផ្លូវ

No menu, no prices, no English. Point, ask, and eat some of the best food in the country.

You
នេះហៅថាអ្វី?
nih hav thaa A-VEI?
What is this called?
Seller
នំបញ្ចុក បង។ ឆ្ងាញ់ណាស់!
num BON-CHOK, bong. chhngañ nas!
Num banh chok. Very tasty!
You
មួយចានប៉ុន្មាន?
muoy CHAAN pon-man?
How much for one plate?
Seller
បីពាន់រៀល។
bei POAN riel.
Three thousand riel.
You
សុំមួយចាន យកទៅផ្ទះ។
som muoy chaan, YOK teuv phteah.
One plate, to take away.
Say It Right

យកទៅផ្ទះ (yok teuv phteah) literally means “take it home” and is how Cambodians say takeaway. Your food arrives in a plastic bag tied with an elastic band.

Street Food Stalls

Key Phrases

Pro-Tip · Follow the Queue

The safest stall is the busiest one — high turnover means nothing sits warm for hours. Look for a crowd of Cambodians rather than a sign in English, and eat where the cooking happens in front of you. Som douch koat — “the same as him” — is the single most useful sentence at a stall, and it usually gets you the thing the regulars actually come for.

ការសុំគិតលុយ

Finished eating. Three words end the meal, and a fourth checks the arithmetic.

You
សុំគិតលុយផង!
som ket LUY phong!
The bill, please!
Waiter
សរុបដប់ប្រាំដុល្លារ។
sa-ROP dop-pram dol-laa.
Fifteen dollars in total.
You
សូមមើលវិក្កយបត្របន្តិច។
som meul vik-KAY-bot bon-tech.

You
បង់តាមកាតបានទេ?
bong taam KAAT baan tei?

som toh, som sach-BRAK.
Sorry, cash only.

គិតលុយ (ket luy) literally means “count the money”. Add phong at the end and a raised hand, and it is warm rather than brusque.

Asking for the Bill

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics

Cashសាច់ប្រាក់sach-brak
I think this is wrong.ខ្ញុំគិតថាខុសkhnyom ket thaa khoh

Pro-Tip · Dollars In, Riel Out

Cambodia runs on two currencies at once. You pay in US dollars and receive change under one dollar in riel, at a fixed rate of about 4,000 riel to the dollar. So a $3.50 bill settled with a $5 note comes back as one dollar and 2,000 riel. Refuse torn or heavily marked dollar notes — shops will refuse them from you later.

Praising & Complaining

ការសរសើរ និងការត្អូញត្អែរ

One compliment will be remembered for months. One complaint, made gently, will be fixed immediately.

You
ឆ្ងាញ់ណាស់! ធ្វើពូកែម៉ែន។
CHHNGAÑ nas! thveu pu-kae maen.
Delicious! Really well made.
Cook
អរគុណ បង។ ញ៉ាំបន្ថែមទេ?
or-KUN, bong. nyam bon-thaem tei?
Thank you. Would you like more?
You
សូមទោស នេះមិនមែនអ្វីដែលខ្ញុំសុំ។
som toh, nih min maen a-vei dael khnyom SOM.
Sorry, this isn’t what I ordered.
Waiter
អូ សូមទោស! ខ្ញុំប្ដូរឲ្យ។
ouh, som TOH! khnyom bdo aoy.
Oh, sorry! I’ll change it.
You
អត់អីទេ អរគុណ។
ot ei TEI, or-kun.
No problem, thank you.
Say It Right

ឆ្ងាញ់ (chhngañ) ends in the ny of canyon, closed off without release. It is the highest praise you can pay a Cambodian cook, and it costs one syllable.

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics

Pro-Tip · Complain Softly, Get More

Raising your voice in a Cambodian restaurant loses you the argument instantly — the staff will smile, freeze, and quietly stop helping. Public anger causes a loss of face on both sides. Open every complaint with som toh, keep your tone flat and friendly, and you will usually get the dish replaced and something free. The soft approach is not politeness here; it is the effective one.

Vegetarian & Allergies

អាហារបួស និងអាឡែស៊ី

“Vegetarian” is not a familiar category here. Be concrete: name what you cannot eat, one item at a time.

You
ខ្ញុំញ៉ាំបួស។ មានម្ហូបបួសទេ?
khnyom nyam BUOH. mien mhoub buoh tei?
I’m vegetarian. Do you have vegetarian food?
Waiter
មាន បន្លែឆា។
MIEN, bon-lae chhaa.
Yes, stir-fried vegetables.
You
កុំដាក់សាច់ និងទឹកត្រី។
kom dak SACH ning tuk-trei.
No meat and no fish sauce.
You
ខ្ញុំមានអាឡែស៊ីនឹងសណ្ដែកដី។
khnyom mien aa-lae-SII neung son-daek-dei.
I’m allergic to peanuts.
Waiter
បាទ ខ្ញុំនឹងប្រាប់ចុងភៅ។
baat, khnyom neung BRAB chong-phov.
Yes, I’ll tell the cook.
Say It Right

បួស (buoh) carries a Buddhist sense — food fit for a monk on holy days. Saying khnyom nyam buoh is understood immediately, where the English word “vegetarian” often is not.

Pro-Tip · Name the Ingredient, Not the Diet

Categories travel badly; ingredients do not. “Vegetarian” may still arrive with chicken stock or a spoon of fish sauce, because those are seasonings rather than meat in the local sense. Say instead: no pork, no chicken, no fish, no fish sauce — four short phrases, listed one by one. For a serious allergy, have a Cambodian friend write it in Khmer on a card and show that; it removes every gap in pronunciation.

Rider
ហាឡូ! ខ្ញុំដល់ហើយ។ ផ្ទះលេខប៉ុន្មាន?

Pro-Tip · Save Your Address in Khmer

Type your address in Khmer script into your phone’s notes once, with the nearest landmark, and paste it into every delivery order afterwards. Riders navigate by landmark plus phone call, not by GPS pin — pins in Phnom Penh are frequently thirty metres and one alley wrong. Adding nov choab … (“next to …”) to the order note saves the call altogether.

A Guest at a Khmer Meal

ជាភ្ញៀវក្នុងអាហារខ្មែរ

You have been invited to eat at a family home. What you say at the table matters more than what you eat.

Host
អញ្ជើញពិសាអាហារ!
an-choeun pi-SAA aa-haa!
Please, help yourself to the food!
You
អរគុណ។ ម្ហូបឆ្ងាញ់ណាស់។
or-kun. mhoub CHHNGAÑ nas.
Thank you. The food is delicious.
Host
ញ៉ាំបន្ថែមទៀតទៅ!
nyam bon-THAEM tiet teuv!
Have some more!
You
ខ្ញុំឆ្អែតហើយ អរគុណច្រើន។
khnyom CHHA-AET haoy, or-kun chraen.
I’m full, thank you very much.
You
អរគុណសម្រាប់ការអញ្ជើញ។
or-kun som-rap kaa an-CHOEUN.

Say It Right

ពិសា (pisaa) is the polite word for to eat, used for guests and elders; ញ៉ាំ (nyam) is the everyday one. Hearing pisaa means you are being honoured.

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
Please, help yourself.អញ្ជើញពិសាan-choeun pi-saa
The food is delicious.ម្ហូបឆ្ងាញ់ណាស់mhoub chhngañ nas

Pro-Tip · Let the Eldest Start

Wait for the oldest person at the table to lift their spoon before you touch yours, and serve them before yourself if a dish is near you. Take small portions from the shared bowls onto your own plate rather than eating out of the middle. You will be pressed to eat more long after you are full — khnyom chha-aet haoy with a hand over the bowl is the accepted way to stop, and it may take saying twice.

31
Shopping & Money

At the Market

នៅផ្សារ

The wet market opens at five and empties by nine. Bring small notes and a bag, and speak first.

You
បង សណ្ដែកបារាំងមួយគីឡូប៉ុន្មាន?
bong, son-daek baa-rang muoy ki-LOU pon-man?
How much is a kilo of potatoes?
Seller
បួនពាន់រៀល បង។
BUON poan riel, bong.
Four thousand riel.
You
សុំពីរគីឡូ។ ស្រស់ទេ?
som pii ki-lou. SROH tei?
Two kilos, please. Is it fresh?
Seller
ស្រស់ណាស់ ទើបមកពីព្រឹក។
SROH nas, teub mok pii pruk.
Very fresh, it came this morning.
You
សុំបន្ថែមម្ទេសបន្តិចផង។
som bon-THAEM mteih bon-tech phong.
Add a few chillies too, please.
Say It Right

Open with bong before the question. Walking up and firing pon-man? at a seller sounds like an interrogation; one warm syllable in front changes the whole exchange.

Ngorn Kakteka65Prepared by Nat Bunchhai

At the Market

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics

Vegetables / fruitបន្លែ / ផ្លែឈើbon-lae / phlae-chheu

Pro-Tip · Find One Seller and Stay

Cambodian markets run on relationships, not on comparison shopping. Buy from the same vegetable seller every week and within a month you will be given the good tomatoes without asking, quoted the local price automatically, and handed free herbs. Learn her name, greet her before you buy, and the market stops being a place you negotiate and becomes a place you are known.

Shopping & Money

Bargaining

ការតថ្លៃ

Bargaining is a conversation, not a fight. Smile the whole way through and be ready to walk.

Seller
ម្ភៃដុល្លារ បង។
MPHEY dol-laa, bong.
Twenty dollars.
You
អូ ថ្លៃណាស់! ចុះថ្លៃបានទេ?
ouh, THLAI nas! choh thlai baan tei?
Oh, that’s expensive! Can you come down?
You
ដប់ដុល្លារបានទេ?
DOP dol-laa baan tei?
Ten dollars, alright?
Seller
មិនបានទេ បង។ ដប់ប្រាំ។
min baan tei, bong. DOP-pram.
Not possible. Fifteen.
You
ដប់ពីរ ខ្ញុំយក។
DOP-pii, khnyom yok.
Twelve and I’ll take it.
Say It Right

The magic word is baan tei? — “is that possible?” Attach it to any number and you have made an offer without ever sounding demanding.

Ngorn Kakteka67Prepared by Nat Bunchhai
Chapter 4 · Shopping & MoneySituation 32
32

Bargaining

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
That’s expensive!ថ្លៃណាស់!thlai nas!
Can you come down?ចុះថ្លៃបានទេ?choh thlai baan tei?
Ten dollars, alright?ដប់ដុល្លារបានទេ?dop dol-laa baan tei?
Cheap / expensiveថោក / ថ្លៃthaok / thlai
I’ll take it.ខ្ញុំយកkhnyom yok
I’ll think about it.ខ្ញុំគិតសិនkhnyom ket sen
What’s your best price?តម្លៃចុងក្រោយប៉ុន្មាន?tom-lai chong-kraoy pon-man?
If I buy two?បើទិញពីរវិញ?baeu tinh pii vinh?
Pro-Tip · Walking Away Is the Real Offer

Say khnyom ket sen — “let me think about it” — and start walking. If your price was workable you will be called back within five steps; if you are not called back, it genuinely was too low. This is understood as part of the game by both sides. What is not acceptable is bargaining hard and then not buying: settle a price only on something you actually intend to take.

Shopping & Money

Asking the Price

ការសួរតម្លៃ

Two words get you a number. The rest of this page teaches you to understand the answer.

You
នេះថ្លៃប៉ុន្មាន?
nih THLAI pon-man?
How much is this?
Seller
មួយម៉ឺនរៀល។
muoy MEUN riel.
Ten thousand riel.
You
សូមទោស ប៉ុន្មានដុល្លារ?
som toh, pon-man DOL-LAA?
Sorry, how much in dollars?
Seller
ពីរដុល្លារកន្លះ។
pii dol-laa KON-LAH.
Two dollars fifty.
You
សូមសរសេរតម្លៃឲ្យខ្ញុំ។
som sor-sei tom-LAI aoy khnyom.
Please write the price down for me.
Say It Right

Riel are quoted in thousands and ten-thousands: muoy poan is 1,000 and មួយម៉ឺន (muoy meun) is 10,000. Miss meun and you will hear the price as ten times too little.

Asking the Price

Phrases

Key Phrases

Pro-Tip · Carry Small Notes

Handing a $50 note to a market seller for a $2 purchase will stop the transaction entirely — nobody at street level holds that much change, and you will be sent to break it yourself. Keep ones, fives and riel notes in a separate pocket. In supermarkets and petrol stations, large notes are fine; everywhere else, the small money is what makes you easy to serve.

Shopping & Money

Clothes, Sizes & Colours

សម្លៀកបំពាក់ ទំហំ និងពណ៌

Sizes run small and there is rarely a changing room. Ask to try, and ask about the colour.

You
សុំមើលអាវនោះបន្តិច។
som meul AAV nuh bon-tech.
May I look at that shirt?
Seller
អញ្ជើញ បង។ ទំហំណា?
an-choeun, bong. TUM-HOM naa?
Please. Which size?
You
សុំធំជាងនេះបន្តិច។
som THOM chieng nih bon-tech.
A bit bigger than this, please.
You
មានពណ៌ខៀវទេ?
mien poa KHIEV tei?
Do you have it in blue?
You
សាកល្បងបានទេ?
saak-LORNG baan tei?
May I try it on?
Say It Right

Comparatives use ជាង (chieng) after the adjective: thom chieng nih — “bigger than this”, literally “big more-than this”.

Ngorn Kakteka71Prepared by Nat Bunchhai

Clothes, Sizes & Colours

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics

Big / smallធំ / តូចthom / touch
A bit bigger, please.សុំធំជាងនេះបន្តិចsom thom chieng nih bon-tech
May I try it on?សាកល្បងបានទេ?saak-lorng baan tei?

Pro-Tip · Have It Altered

Tailoring is cheap and everywhere. A market shirt that almost fits can be taken in for a dollar or two by the ជាងកាត់ដេរ (chieng kat-dei, tailor) sitting three stalls away — often on the spot. This is why Cambodians buy clothes that are slightly loose rather than slightly tight, and why thom chieng nih bon-tech is the more useful of the two size phrases above.

Shopping & Money

At the Minimart

នៅហាងលក់ទំនិញ

Fixed prices, air conditioning, and one question you will ask constantly: where is it?

You
សូមទោស មានទឹកសុទ្ធធំទេ?
som toh, mien tuk SOT thom tei?
Excuse me, do you have large bottled water?
Staff
មាន នៅជួរខាងក្រោយ។
MIEN, nov chuo khang-kraoy.
Yes, in the row at the back.
You
សាប៊ូនៅជួរណា?
saa-BUU nov chuo naa?
Which aisle is the soap in?
Staff
ជួរទីពីរ បង។
chuo ti PII, bong.
Aisle two.
You
មិនបាច់ថង់ទេ អរគុណ។
min bach THONG tei, or-kun.
No bag needed, thank you.
Say It Right

មាន … ទេ? (mien … tei?) — “do you have …?” — is the workhorse shopping question. Slot any noun into the middle and you can shop anywhere in the country.

At the Minimart

Phrases

Pro-Tip · Check the Date on Dairy

Power cuts are common and the cold chain is not always unbroken, so milk, yoghurt and imported cheese deserve a glance at the date — ផុតកំណត់ (phot kom-not), “expiry”. Minimart prices are fixed and marked, so no bargaining happens here; that is precisely what makes them a comfortable place to practise your Khmer without any money riding on the outcome.

Shopping & Money

At the Pharmacy

នៅឱសថស្ថាន

Pharmacists here diagnose as well as dispense. Describe the symptom simply and let them suggest.

You
ខ្ញុំឈឺក្បាល និងក្ដៅខ្លួន។
khnyom chheu KBAAL ning kdav kluon.
I have a headache and a fever.
Pharmacist
ប៉ុន្មានថ្ងៃហើយ?
pon-man THNGAI haoy?
For how many days?
You
ពីរថ្ងៃហើយ។
PII thngai haoy.
Two days now.
Pharmacist
ញ៉ាំមួយគ្រាប់ បីដងក្នុងមួយថ្ងៃ។
nyam muoy KROAB, bei dong knong muoy thngai.
Take one tablet, three times a day.
You
ញ៉ាំមុន ឬក្រោយអាហារ?
nyam MUN reu kraoy aa-haa?
Before or after food?
Say It Right

ឈឺ (chheu) means “to hurt / be sick” and takes the body part straight after it: chheu kbaal (head), chheu poh (stomach), chheu thmenh (tooth).

At the Pharmacy

Phrases

Key Phrases

Pro-Tip · Ask for the Box

Cambodian pharmacies often dispense loose tablets in a small plastic bag with the dosage written on it, and antibiotics are sold without a prescription. Ask for the original box so you can read the drug name and strength — som yok bratab phong, “the packet too, please”. If symptoms last more than three days, or involve a high fever, go to a clinic rather than back to the pharmacy: dengue is common and needs a blood test.

Shopping & Money

Riel & Dollars

រៀល និងដុល្លារ

Two currencies, one wallet. Understand the exchange and you stop losing small amounts all day long.

You
ខ្ញុំចង់ប្ដូរលុយ។
khnyom chong BDO luy.
I want to change money.
Changer
ប្ដូរប៉ុន្មានដុល្លារ?
bdo pon-man DOL-LAA?
How many dollars?
You
ហាសិបដុល្លារ។ អត្រាប៉ុន្មាន?
haa-sep dol-laa. AT-TRAA pon-man?
Fifty dollars. What’s the rate?
Changer
មួយដុល្លារបួនពាន់រៀល។
muoy dol-laa BUON poan riel.
Four thousand riel to the dollar.
You
សុំលុយតូចៗផង។
som luy TOUCH-touch phong.
Small notes, please.
Say It Right

លុយតូចៗ (luy touch-touch) — literally “small small money” — is how you ask for small denominations. It is the most practically useful request on this page.

Riel & Dollars

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
I want to change money.ខ្ញុំចង់ប្ដូរលុយkhnyom chong bdo luy

Riel / dollarsរៀល / ដុល្លារriel / dol-laa

Pro-Tip · The 4,000 Rule

The rate is pegged at roughly 4,000 riel to one dollar and barely moves, so the arithmetic is easy: 2,000 riel is fifty cents, 10,000 riel is $2.50. Dollars handle the large amounts, riel handles everything under a dollar — there are no US coins in circulation at all. Torn or ink-marked dollar bills are routinely refused, so inspect the notes you are given before you walk away.

Ngorn Kakteka78Prepared by Nat Bunchhai

Bank & ATM Problems

បញ្ហាធនាគារ និងម៉ាស៊ីនអេធីអឹម

The machine swallowed your card, or refuses to pay. Go inside and explain it in five sentences.

You
សូមទោស ម៉ាស៊ីនលេបកាតខ្ញុំ។
som toh, maa-sin LEIP kaat khnyom.
Excuse me, the machine swallowed my card.
Teller
សុំមើលលិខិតឆ្លងដែនបន្តិច។
som meul li-khet CHHLONG-daen bon-tech.
May I see your passport?
You
នេះបាទ។ ខ្ញុំដកលុយមិនបាន។
nih baat. khnyom DOK luy min baan.
Here. I couldn’t withdraw money.
Teller
សុំចាំម្ភៃនាទី។
som cham MPHEY nie-ti.
Please wait twenty minutes.
You
គិតកម្រៃប៉ុន្មាន?
ket kom-RAI pon-man?
How much is the fee?
Say It Right

ដក (dok) is “to withdraw” and ដាក់ (dak) is “to deposit / put in”. One vowel apart, opposite meanings — worth drilling before you stand at a counter.

Bank & ATM Problems

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
Bankធនាគារthie-nie-kie
I want to withdraw money.ខ្ញុំចង់ដកលុយkhnyom chong dok luy

The ATM is out of order.ម៉ាស៊ីនខូចmaa-sin khouch

Transfer moneyផ្ទេរប្រាក់phtei brak
My card doesn’t work.កាតខ្ញុំប្រើមិនបានkaat khnyom braeu min baan
Pro-Tip · Withdraw Dollars, Not Riel

Most Cambodian ATMs let you choose the currency. Take dollars — riel withdrawals come out in large notes that small shops cannot break. Machines also charge a flat fee of around $4 to $5 per withdrawal regardless of amount, so take out more, less often. Choose an ATM inside a bank branch during opening hours: if it eats your card at 9 p.m. on a Friday, nobody can open it until Monday.

Shopping & Money

SIM Cards & Top-Up

ស៊ីមកាត និងការបញ្ចូលទឹកប្រាក់

A local SIM costs a couple of dollars and changes everything. Buy it from a shop, not a street table.

You
ខ្ញុំចង់ទិញស៊ីមកាតមួយ។
khnyom chong tinh SIM-kaat muoy.
I’d like to buy a SIM card.
Staff
សុំលិខិតឆ្លងដែនផង។
som li-khet CHHLONG-daen phong.
Your passport, please.
You
មានកញ្ចប់អ៊ីនធឺណិតទេ?
mien kon-chop in-thoe-NET tei?
Do you have an internet package?
Staff
មួយខែប្រាំដុល្លារ។
muoy khae PRAM dol-laa.
Five dollars a month.
You
សុំបញ្ចូលទឹកប្រាក់ដប់ដុល្លារ។
som banh-CHOUL tuk-brak dop dol-laa.
Please top up ten dollars.
Say It Right

Topping up is បញ្ចូលទឹកប្រាក់ (banh-choul tuk-brak) — literally “pour in water-money”. Shops with a phone-company sign outside will do it in fifteen seconds.

SIM Cards & Top-Up

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
SIM cardស៊ីមកាតsim-kaat
Please top up …សុំបញ្ចូលទឹកប្រាក់ …som banh-choul tuk-brak …

Pro-Tip · Buy It in the Shop, Not the Street

SIM registration is legally tied to a passport, and a card sold pre-registered under a stranger’s name can be cut off without warning. Go to a branded Smart, Cellcard or Metfone shop, hand over your passport, and have them register it to you. Data is extremely cheap by international standards — a few dollars buys a generous monthly package — and coverage is good in towns, patchy on rural roads.

Returns & Exchanges

ការប្ដូរ និងសងទំនិញវិញ

Refunds are rare; exchanges are usually possible. Keep the receipt and go back quickly.

You
ខ្ញុំចង់ប្ដូរអាវនេះ។
khnyom chong BDO aav nih.
I’d like to exchange this shirt.
Staff
មានបង្កាន់ដៃទេ?
mien bong-KAN-dai tei?
Do you have the receipt?
You
មាន នេះបាទ។ វាតូចពេក។
mien, nih baat. vie TOUCH peik.
Yes, here. It’s too small.
Staff
ប្ដូរបាន តែសងលុយវិញមិនបានទេ។
BDO baan, tae song luy vinh min baan tei.
Exchange yes, but no refund.
You
អញ្ចឹងសុំធំជាងនេះ។
an-choeng som THOM chieng nih.
Then a bigger one, please.
Say It Right

ប្ដូរ (bdo) is “to exchange”; សងលុយវិញ (song luy vinh) is “to give the money back”. Ask for the first — the second rarely exists here.

Pro-Tip · Test It Before You Leave

There is no legal right to return goods you simply changed your mind about, and most small shops operate on “sold is sold”. So test everything at the counter: plug in the charger, switch on the fan, check both shoes, unfold the whole garment. Electronics from proper stores carry a genuine ធានា (thie-nie, guarantee) — keep that slip somewhere safe, because without it repairs are charged in full.

Accommodation & Home

Checking In

ការចុះឈ្មោះចូលស្នាក់នៅ

Arriving at a guesthouse with no booking. Ask to see the room before you agree to anything.

You
មានបន្ទប់ទំនេរទេ?
mien bon-TUP tum-nei tei?
Do you have a free room?
Staff
មាន បាទ។ ស្នាក់ប៉ុន្មានយប់?
MIEN, baat. snak pon-man yub?
Yes. How many nights?
You
បីយប់។ មួយយប់ថ្លៃប៉ុន្មាន?
bei yub. muoy yub THLAI pon-man?
Three nights. How much per night?
Staff
ដប់ប្រាំដុល្លារ មានម៉ាស៊ីនត្រជាក់។
dop-pram dol-laa, mien maa-sin tro-CHEAK.
Fifteen dollars, with air conditioning.
You
សុំមើលបន្ទប់សិនបានទេ?
som MEUL bon-tup sen baan tei?
May I see the room first?
Say It Right

សិន (sen) at the end of a request means “first, before anything else”. som meul … sen is the polite way to inspect before committing.

Checking In

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
Do you have a free room?មានបន្ទប់ទំនេរទេ?mien bon-tup tum-nei tei?
How much per night?មួយយប់ថ្លៃប៉ុន្មាន?muoy yub thlai pon-man?
Three nightsបីយប់bei yub

May I see the room first?សុំមើលបន្ទប់សិនបានទេ?som meul bon-tup sen baan tei?

Pro-Tip · Always Ask to See It

Inspecting the room before agreeing is completely normal and nobody is offended by it — guesthouses expect it. Check three things: that the air conditioning actually blows cold, that hot water reaches the shower, and that the window does not open onto a karaoke bar. Rooms on the same floor at the same price often differ enormously, and asking to see a second one usually gets you the better of the two.

Hotel Requests & Problems

ការស្នើសុំ និងបញ្ហាបន្ទប់

Something is not working. Report it at reception in one sentence and it is usually fixed within the hour.

You
បន្ទប់ខ្ញុំគ្មានទឹកក្ដៅទេ។
bon-tup khnyom kmien tuk-KDAV tei.
My room has no hot water.
Staff
សុំទោស បន្ទប់លេខប៉ុន្មាន?
som toh, bon-tup LEIK pon-man?
Sorry, which room number?
You
លេខម្ភៃបី។ ហើយវ៉ាយហ្វាយក៏ខូចដែរ។
leik MPHEY-bei. haoy wai-fai kâ khouch dae.
Twenty-three. And the Wi-Fi is broken too.
You
សុំខ្នើយបន្ថែមមួយផង។
som KHNOEY bon-thaem muoy phong.

Yes, I’ll come up now.

គ្មាន … ទេ (kmien … tei) means “there isn’t any …”. It is the negative twin of mien … tei? and reports a missing thing without blaming anybody.

Pro-Tip · Report It the Same Day

Saying nothing and then complaining at checkout gets you nowhere; reporting a fault immediately almost always gets it fixed or gets you moved. Keep the tone light — a problem raised with a smile is a favour asked, and a favour asked is a favour granted. Power cuts are frequent in the provinces, so a guesthouse with a ម៉ាស៊ីនភ្លើង (maa-sin phleung, generator) is worth a dollar or two more per night.

Leaving early, storing a bag, and checking the bill for things you did not drink.

khnyom chong CHENH thngai nih.
I’d like to check out today.

Pro-Tip · Luggage Storage Is Free

Nearly every guesthouse will hold your bag for the day after checkout at no charge, which turns an awkward afternoon before a night bus into a free one. Ask with phnhaeu kaa-boub tuk baan tei? and take anything valuable with you. Tipping is not expected in Cambodian hotels, but leaving a couple of dollars for the cleaner is quietly appreciated and very unusual.

Viewing a flat. Ask about the rent, the deposit and — most importantly — the electricity rate.

Pro-Tip · The Electricity Rate Is the Real Rent

Landlords in Cambodia commonly resell electricity at well above the state rate, and with air conditioning running you can add a hundred dollars a month without noticing. Always ask the price per unit and compare it against the official EDC tariff before signing. Two months’ deposit is standard, and getting it back at the end depends almost entirely on the relationship you build — so photograph the whole flat on the day you move in.

Talking to the Landlord

ការនិយាយជាមួយម្ចាស់ផ្ទះ

Rent day, a broken tap, and a request. Keep it warm — your landlord is also your neighbour.

You
នេះថ្លៃឈ្នួលខែនេះ បង។
nih thlai CHHNUOL khae nih, bong.
Here’s this month’s rent.
Landlord
អរគុណ។ មានបញ្ហាអ្វីទេ?
or-kun. mien bon-HAA a-vei tei?
Thank you. Any problems?
You
ក្បាលទឹកក្នុងបន្ទប់ទឹកលេច។
kbaal TUK knong bon-tup-tuk leich.
The tap in the bathroom is leaking.
Landlord
ខ្ញុំនឹងហៅជាងថ្ងៃស្អែក។
khnyom neung HAV chieng thngai sa-aek.
I’ll call a repairman tomorrow.
You
សុំបង្កាន់ដៃផង បង។
som bong-KAN-dai phong, bong.
A receipt, please.
Say It Right

Call your landlord bong if they are near your age, om if they are your parents’ generation. Getting this right shapes the entire relationship — and the relationship is what gets things repaired.

A receipt, please.សុំបង្កាន់ដៃផងsom bong-kan-dai phong

I want to renew the contract.ខ្ញុំចង់បន្តកិច្ចសន្យាkhnyom chong bon-tor kech-son-yie
I’m moving out next month.ខ្ញុំនឹងចេញខែក្រោយkhnyom neung chenh khae kraoy
Pro-Tip · Give a Month’s Notice, in Person

Contracts here are often short and informally enforced, so what protects you is goodwill rather than paperwork. Announce a departure a full month ahead and face to face, never by message, and pay the last month rather than asking to have it taken from the deposit — that single gesture is what usually gets the deposit returned. A small gift at Khmer New Year does more for your tenancy than any clause.

Ngorn Kakteka95Prepared by Nat Bunchhai

Accommodation & Home

Electricity, Water & Wi-Fi

ភ្លើង ទឹក និងអ៊ីនធឺណិត

The power is out and the bill looks wrong. Two conversations you will have more than once.

You
ភ្លើងរលត់តាំងពីព្រឹក។
PHLEUNG ro-lot tang pii pruk.
The power has been off since morning.
Landlord
ទាំងផ្លូវនេះដាច់ភ្លើង។
teang PHLOV nih dach phleung.
The whole street has a power cut.
You
វិក្កយបត្រខែនេះថ្លៃជាងធម្មតា។
vik-kay-bot khae nih THLAI chieng thoam-ma-daa.
This month’s bill is higher than usual.
Landlord
ខ្ញុំនឹងពិនិត្យមាទ្រនិចឡើងវិញ។
khnyom neung pi-NET maa-tro-nech laeung vinh.
I’ll check the meter again.
You
អ៊ីនធឺណិតដាច់ជាញឹកញាប់។
in-thoe-net DACH chie nheuk-nheap.
The internet cuts out often.
Say It Right

ដាច់ (dach) means “cut off” and applies to power, water, internet and roads alike: dach phleung, dach tuk, dach phlov.

Ngorn Kakteka96Prepared by Nat Bunchhai

Electricity, Water & Wi-Fi

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics

Meterមាទ្រនិចmaa-tro-nech

Pro-Tip · Photograph the Meter

Take a picture of the electricity meter on the day you move in and on the first of every month. It costs ten seconds and settles every billing dispute instantly, because you can show the reading rather than argue about it. Keep a torch and a power bank charged: cuts of two or three hours are ordinary, especially in the hot season when the whole city runs its air conditioning at once.

Accommodation & Home

Calling a Repairman

ការហៅជាងជួសជុល

Something has broken. Name the thing, say it is broken, and agree the price before he starts.

You
ម៉ាស៊ីនត្រជាក់ខ្ញុំខូច។
maa-sin tro-cheak khnyom KHOUCH.
My air conditioner is broken.
Repairman
វាមិនត្រជាក់ ឬមិនដើរ?
vie min tro-cheak reu min DAEU?
Is it not cold, or not running at all?
You
ដើរ តែមិនត្រជាក់។
DAEU, tae min tro-cheak.
It runs, but it isn’t cold.
Repairman
ត្រូវបញ្ចូលឧស្ម័ន ម្ភៃដុល្លារ។
trov banh-choul OS-MAN, mphey dol-laa.
It needs regassing, twenty dollars.
You
មកបានពេលណា?
mok baan PEIL naa?
When can you come?
Say It Right

ខូច (khouch) covers every kind of broken — machines, phones, roads, even food that has gone off. Point at the thing and say it; you will be understood.

Ngorn Kakteka98Prepared by Nat Bunchhai
Chapter 5 · Accommodation & HomeSituation 47
47

Calling a Repairman

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics

Repairman / technicianជាងជួសជុលchieng chuoh-chul

Pro-Tip · Agree the Price Before He Opens It

Once a machine is in pieces on your floor your negotiating position has gone. Ask chuoh-chul oh pon-man? at the door, and ask again if he discovers a second fault. Most repairmen are found by asking your neighbours rather than searching online — the one who fixed the flat downstairs will come faster, charge the local rate and care about his reputation on your street.

Accommodation & Home

Hiring a Cleaner

ការជួលអ្នកសម្អាតផ្ទះ

Agreeing days, hours and pay. Be clear and generous at the start; it is far easier than adjusting later.

You
ខ្ញុំត្រូវការអ្នកសម្អាតផ្ទះ។
khnyom trov-kaa neak som-AT phteah.
I need someone to clean the house.
Cleaner
មួយអាទិត្យប៉ុន្មានដង?
muoy aa-tit pon-man DONG?
How many times a week?
You
ពីរដង ថ្ងៃច័ន្ទ និងថ្ងៃសុក្រ។
PII dong, thngai chan ning thngai sok.
Twice — Monday and Friday.
Cleaner
មួយដងដប់ដុល្លារ បានទេ?
muoy dong DOP dol-laa, baan tei?
Ten dollars a visit, alright?
You
បានហើយ។ ខ្ញុំបង់ចុងខែ។
BAAN haoy. khnyom bong chong khae.
Agreed. I’ll pay at month’s end.
Say It Right

Days of the week all begin with ថ្ងៃ (thngai): thngai chan Monday, thngai ong-kie Tuesday, thngai sok Friday, thngai aa-tit Sunday.

Ngorn Kakteka100Prepared by Nat Bunchhai

Hiring a Cleaner

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
To cleanសម្អាតsom-at

Pro-Tip · Pay Well and Pay on Time

Domestic work is often the household’s main income, and a day’s pay missed matters. Agree the rate openly at the start, pay on the day you promised, and add a month’s wage as a bonus at Khmer New Year — this is expected of good employers, not optional generosity. Praise directly and correct gently; criticism given in front of anyone else causes real loss of face and is rarely recovered from.

Accommodation & Home

Neighbours & Security

អ្នកជិតខាង និងសន្តិសុខ

Introducing yourself to the people on your street, and to the guard who watches it at night.

You
ជម្រាបសួរ ខ្ញុំទើបមកនៅថ្មី។
chom-riep suor, khnyom teub mok nov THMEI.
Hello, I’ve just moved in.
Neighbour
អូ! សូមស្វាគមន៍ បង។
ouh! som svie-KOM, bong.
Oh! Welcome.
You
ខ្ញុំនៅផ្ទះលេខដប់ពីរ។
khnyom nov phteah leik DOP-pii.
I live at number twelve.
You
ឆ្មាំបិទច្រកទ្វារម៉ោងប៉ុន្មាន?
CHHMAM bet chrok-tvie maong pon-man?
What time does the guard lock the gate?
Neighbour
ម៉ោងដប់មួយយប់។
maong DOP-muoy yub.
Eleven at night.
Say It Right

សូមស្វាគមន៍ (som svie-kom) is “welcome”. You will hear it constantly — at doors, at shops, and on every hotel sign in the country.

Ngorn Kakteka102Prepared by Nat Bunchhai

Neighbours & Security

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
Neighbourអ្នកជិតខាងneak chit-khang
I’ve just moved in.ខ្ញុំទើបមកនៅថ្មីkhnyom teub mok nov thmei

Security guardឆ្មាំchhmam
Gate / lockច្រកទ្វារ / សោchrok-tvie / sao
Please keep the noise down.សូមបន្ថយសំឡេងបន្តិចsom bon-thoy som-leng bon-tech
I’ll be away a few days.ខ្ញុំទៅឆ្ងាយពីរបីថ្ងៃkhnyom teuv chhngay pii-bei thngai
Could you keep an eye on my house?ជួយមើលផ្ទះខ្ញុំផងchuoy meul phteah khnyom phong
Pro-Tip · Your Street Is Your Security System

Introduce yourself to the neighbours and the chhmam in your first week, and greet them every single day afterwards. On a Cambodian street, people watch out for those they know by name — the guard who has been handed a cold drink on a hot afternoon will notice a stranger at your gate. Weddings and funerals on the street are loud and go on for days; complaining about them marks you out, while attending for ten minutes makes you a neighbour.

Ngorn Kakteka103Prepared by Nat Bunchhai

Laundry

ការបោកគក់

Laundry is sold by the kilo and comes back folded. Say what must not go in the dryer.

You
បោកគក់មួយគីឡូប៉ុន្មាន?
baok-kok muoy ki-LOU pon-man?
How much per kilo for washing?
Staff
មួយពាន់រៀល រួមទាំងអ៊ុត។
muoy poan riel, ruom teang UT.
One thousand riel, ironing included.
You
ពេលណាបានយក?
peil naa baan YOK?
When can I collect it?
Staff
ថ្ងៃស្អែករសៀល។
thngai sa-aek ro-SIEL.
Tomorrow afternoon.
You
អាវនេះកុំដាក់ម៉ាស៊ីនសម្ងួត។
aav nih kom dak maa-sin som-NGUOT.
Don’t put this shirt in the dryer.
Say It Right

បោកគក់ (baok-kok) is the everyday word for doing laundry. Shops advertise it on hand-painted signs alongside the price per kilo.

Pro-Tip · Count It In and Count It Out

Laundry shops wash several households together, so socks and single shirts do migrate. Count the items as you hand them over — the staff will happily count with you, and it is entirely normal — then count them again on collection. In the rainy season, clothes may come back not quite dry and smelling of it; a shop with a proper ម៉ាស៊ីនសម្ងួត (maa-sin som-nguot, dryer) is worth walking an extra street for.

Health & Emergencies

Describing Symptoms

ការរៀបរាប់រោគសញ្ញា

One verb — chheu — plus a body part covers most of what you need to say when you are unwell.

Nurse
ឈឺត្រង់ណា?
CHHEU trong naa?
Where does it hurt?
You
ខ្ញុំឈឺពោះ និងក្ដៅខ្លួន។
khnyom chheu POH ning kdav kluon.
My stomach hurts and I have a fever.
Nurse
ចាប់ផ្ដើមពីពេលណា?
chap-PHDAEUM pii peil naa?
When did it start?
You
តាំងពីម្សិលមិញ។ ខ្ញុំក៏ក្អួតដែរ។
tang pii msel-minh. khnyom kâ KA-UOT dae.
Since yesterday. I’ve been vomiting too.
You
ខ្ញុំវិលមុខពេលក្រោកឈរ។
khnyom VIL muk peil kraok chho.
I feel dizzy when I stand up.
Say It Right

ក្ដៅខ្លួន (kdav kluon) is literally “hot body” — a fever. Do not say khnyom kdav alone; that just means you are feeling warm.

Ngorn Kakteka107Prepared by Nat Bunchhai
Chapter 6 · Health & EmergenciesSituation 51
51

Describing Symptoms

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
Where does it hurt?ឈឺត្រង់ណា?chheu trong naa?
Head / stomach / throatក្បាល / ពោះ / បំពង់កkbaal / poh / bom-pong-kor
I have a fever.ខ្ញុំក្ដៅខ្លួនkhnyom kdav kluon
I’m coughing.ខ្ញុំក្អកkhnyom ka-ak
I’ve been vomiting.ខ្ញុំក្អួតkhnyom ka-uot
I feel dizzy.ខ្ញុំវិលមុខkhnyom vil muk
I have a cold / flu.ខ្ញុំផ្ដាសាយkhnyom phdaa-say
Since yesterdayតាំងពីម្សិលមិញtang pii msel-minh
Pro-Tip · Fever Plus Aches Means a Blood Test

Dengue is common across Cambodia and its early signs look exactly like flu: high fever, headache behind the eyes, deep muscle ache. If a fever lasts more than two days, go to a clinic and ask for a blood test rather than taking more paracetamol — and avoid ibuprofen or aspirin, which are dangerous in dengue. Say khnyom chong pinet chhiem: “I want a blood test.”

Ngorn Kakteka108Prepared by Nat Bunchhai

Health & Emergencies

At the Doctor

នៅជួបគ្រូពេទ្យ

Registering at a clinic, being examined, and asking the two questions that matter most.

You
ខ្ញុំចង់ជួបគ្រូពេទ្យ។
khnyom chong chuop kruu-PEIT.
I’d like to see a doctor.
Doctor
សុំពិនិត្យបន្តិច។ ដកដង្ហើមវែងៗ។
som pi-NET bon-tech. dok dong-haeum veng-veng.
Let me examine you. Breathe deeply.
You
តើខ្ញុំកើតជំងឺអ្វី?
tae khnyom kaeut chum-NGEU a-vei?
What illness do I have?
Doctor
ត្រូវពិនិត្យឈាមសិន។
trov pi-net CHHIEM sen.
We need a blood test first.
You
អស់ថ្លៃប៉ុន្មាន? មានធានារ៉ាប់រងទេ?
oh THLAI pon-man? mien thie-nie-rap-rong tei?
How much will it cost? Do you take insurance?
Say It Right

គ្រូពេទ្យ (kruu-peit) is a doctor; មន្ទីរពេទ្យ (mon-ti-peit) is a hospital. Both contain peit, the root for medicine.

Pro-Tip · Know Your Nearest Good Clinic Now

Find out today — before you need it — which clinic in your town handles foreigners, and save the number. In Phnom Penh and Siem Reap there are international clinics with English-speaking doctors; in the provinces, standards vary a great deal and serious cases are often evacuated to the capital or to Bangkok. If you are staying long term, medical insurance that covers evacuation is the single most valuable thing you can buy.

Ngorn Kakteka110Prepared by Nat Bunchhai

Health & Emergencies

At the Dentist

នៅពេទ្យធ្មេញ

Dentistry here is good and inexpensive. Point at the tooth and say how long it has hurt.

You
ខ្ញុំឈឺធ្មេញខាងក្រោយ។
khnyom chheu THMENH khang-kraoy.
My back tooth hurts.
Dentist
ឈឺប៉ុន្មានថ្ងៃហើយ?
chheu pon-man THNGAI haoy?
How many days has it hurt?
You
មួយអាទិត្យហើយ។ ឈឺពេលញ៉ាំត្រជាក់។
muoy AA-TIT haoy. chheu peil nyam tro-cheak.
A week. It hurts with cold things.
Dentist
ធ្មេញពុក ត្រូវឧបធ្មេញ។
thmenh PUK, trov op thmenh.
It’s decayed; it needs a filling.
You
សុំកុំដកធ្មេញបានទេ?
som kom DOK thmenh baan tei?
Can you avoid pulling it?
Say It Right

ធ្មេញ (thmenh) begins with a puffed t pressed straight into m — one syllable, no vowel between. Say “t-menh”, not “ta-menh”.

At the Dentist

Key Phrases

Pro-Tip · Dental Work Is a Bargain

Cambodia has a large number of well-trained dentists, many educated abroad, and prices are a fraction of Western ones — a cleaning costs a few dollars, a filling perhaps twenty. Foreigners living here often schedule dental work deliberately during their stay. Choose a clinic that shows you sterile packaging opened in front of you, and ask what the total will be before treatment starts, not after.

Health & Emergencies

Medicine & Dosage

ថ្នាំ និងកម្រិតប្រើ

Getting the instructions right. Repeat the dosage back — it is the safest thing you can do.

Pharmacist
ញ៉ាំមួយគ្រាប់ព្រឹក និងល្ងាច។
nyam muoy KROAB pruk ning lngiech.
One tablet morning and evening.
You
ព្រឹកមួយ ល្ងាចមួយ មែនទេ?
pruk muoy, lngiech muoy, MAEN tei?
One in the morning, one in the evening — correct?
Pharmacist
ត្រូវហើយ ញ៉ាំក្រោយអាហារ។
TROV haoy, nyam kraoy aa-haa.
Correct, after food.
You
ញ៉ាំប៉ុន្មានថ្ងៃ?
nyam pon-man THNGAI?
For how many days?
You
មានផលរំខានទេ?
mien PHOL rom-khan tei?
Are there side effects?
Say It Right

Repeat instructions back with … maen tei? — “correct?”. It turns a one-way instruction into a confirmed one, and pharmacists appreciate it.

Pro-Tip · Finish the Antibiotics

Antibiotics are sold freely here and are often handed out for ordinary colds, which they do nothing for. If you are genuinely prescribed a course, finish all of it even once you feel well — stopping early is how resistant infections are bred, and Southeast Asia already has a serious problem with them. Also check every packet’s expiry date at the counter: stock rotation in small pharmacies is not always careful.

Calling for Help

ការស្រែកសុំជំនួយ

The page you hope never to need. Learn the first three lines by heart, tonight.

You
ជួយផង! មានគ្រោះថ្នាក់!
CHUOY phong! mien kroh-thnak!
Help! There’s been an accident!
You
សូមហៅរថយន្តសង្គ្រោះ!
som hav ro-TEAH song-kroh!
Please call an ambulance!
Passer-by
មានរឿងអ្វី? នៅឯណា?
mien ROEUNG a-vei? nov ae-naa?
What happened? Where?
You
មនុស្សម្នាក់របួសធ្ងន់។
mo-nuh mneak ro-BUOH thngon.
Someone is badly injured.
You
មន្ទីរពេទ្យជិតបំផុតនៅឯណា?
mon-ti-peit CHIT bom-phot nov ae-naa?
Where is the nearest hospital?
Say It Right

ជួយផង! (chuoy phong!) is the shout for help. Two syllables, loud, repeated — this is the one phrase in the book to memorise before you need to look it up.

Ngorn Kakteka115Prepared by Nat Bunchhai

Key Phrases

Pro-Tip · Get to the Hospital Yourself

Ambulance coverage is limited and slow outside the capital, and in a real emergency Cambodians drive the patient in themselves — by car, by tuk-tuk, by motorbike. Do the same rather than waiting. Keep three things written in Khmer in your wallet or phone: your blood type, any allergy, and the name of the nearest hospital. The national emergency numbers are 119 for ambulance, 117 for police and 118 for fire.

Reporting a Theft

ការរាយការណ៍ពីការលួច

Your bag is gone. You need a police report for the insurance, so go the same day.

You
មានចោរលួចកាបូបខ្ញុំ។
mien CHAO luoch kaa-boub khnyom.
A thief stole my bag.
Officer
កើតឡើងនៅឯណា ពេលណា?
kaeut laeung nov AE-NAA, peil naa?
Where and when did it happen?
You
នៅមុខផ្សារ ម៉ោងប្រាំល្ងាច។
nov muk PHSAA, maong pram lngiech.
In front of the market, at five in the evening.
You
ក្នុងនោះមានលិខិតឆ្លងដែន និងលុយ។
knong nuh mien li-khet CHHLONG-daen ning luy.
It had my passport and money in it.
You
ខ្ញុំត្រូវការរបាយការណ៍សម្រាប់ធានារ៉ាប់រង។
khnyom trov-kaa ro-bay-KAA som-rap thie-nie-rap-rong.
I need a report for my insurance.
Say It Right

លួច (luoch) is “to steal” and បាត់ (bat) is “to be lost”. Choose carefully: one is a crime report, the other is a lost-property enquiry.

Pro-Tip · Bag Snatching From Motorbikes

The commonest crime against foreigners in Phnom Penh is a bag pulled from a passing motorbike, which can drag you into the road. Carry bags on the side away from traffic, or across your body under an arm, and never hold a phone loosely at the kerb. If it happens, let go — a bag is replaceable. Report it the same day; the station will write a report, sometimes for a small unofficial fee, and insurers require it.

A Traffic Accident

គ្រោះថ្នាក់ចរាចរណ៍

A minor collision. Stay calm, check for injuries, and do not admit fault before anyone arrives.

You
អ្នករបួសទេ?
neak ro-BUOH tei?
Are you injured?
Rider
អត់ទេ តែម៉ូតូខូច។
ot tei, tae moto KHOUCH.
No, but my motorbike is damaged.
You
សូមហៅប៉ូលិសមកសិន។
som hav POU-LIH mok sen.
Let’s call the police first.
You
ខ្ញុំនឹងថតរូបទុក។
khnyom neung THOT ruup tuk.
I’ll take photographs.
You
សុំលេខទូរស័ព្ទ និងអត្តសញ្ញាណប័ណ្ណ។
som leik tuu-ra-sap ning at-ta-son-NHAN-ban.
Your phone number and ID card, please.
Say It Right

Ask neak ro-buoh tei? — “are you injured?” — before anything else. Beginning with concern rather than blame changes how the entire situation unfolds.

A Traffic Accident

Phrases

Key Phrases

Are you injured?អ្នករបួសទេ?neak ro-buoh tei?

Pro-Tip · Fault Follows the Larger Vehicle

In practice, responsibility here is often assigned to whoever was driving the bigger vehicle — and to the foreigner, who is assumed able to pay. Disputes are usually settled on the spot with cash rather than through insurers. Stay calm, never raise your voice, photograph everything including both number plates, and phone a Khmer-speaking friend to negotiate for you. Above all, do not drive away: leaving the scene turns a claim into a criminal matter.

Massage & Spa

ម៉ាស្សា និងស្ប៉ា

Khmer massage is firm. Learn “gently” and “too strong” before you lie down, not during.

Staff
ម៉ាស្សាខ្មែរ ឬម៉ាស្សាប្រេង?
maa-saa KHMAE reu maa-saa breng?
Khmer massage or oil massage?
You
ម៉ាស្សាខ្មែរ មួយម៉ោង។
maa-saa KHMAE, muoy maong.
Khmer massage, one hour.
You
សូមធ្វើថ្នមៗបន្តិច។
som thveu THNOM-thnom bon-tech.
Please do it gently.
You
ខ្លាំងពេក! ឈឺ។
KHLANG peik! chheu.
Too strong! It hurts.
You
សូមផ្ដោតលើស្មា។
som PHDAOT leu smaa.
Please focus on my shoulders.
Say It Right

ថ្នមៗ (thnom-thnom) means “gently, softly”, and ខ្លាំង (khlang) means “strong”. Between them you can steer any massage in the country.

Pro-Tip · Look for the Blind Massage Centres

Cambodia has a network of training centres employing blind and partially sighted therapists, and the standard of traditional Khmer massage there is generally excellent — firm, technical, and priced at a few dollars an hour. Seeing Hands is the best known. A tip of a dollar or two is genuinely appreciated. Note that Khmer massage involves stretching and deep pressure rather than oil and gliding; thnom-thnom is not a sign of weakness, it is useful information.

នៅកន្លែងហាត់ប្រាណ

Joining a gym, asking about the monthly rate, and learning the words for the classes on the wall.

You
សមាជិកមួយខែថ្លៃប៉ុន្មាន?

Pro-Tip · Exercise at Dawn or Dusk

Cambodians train early and late, never in the middle of the day — by ten in the morning the heat makes outdoor exercise genuinely risky. Head to any riverside or public park at around six in the evening and you will find free open-air aerobics classes, dozens of people following an instructor with a speaker, for a few hundred riel or nothing at all. It is the friendliest possible way to practise both your fitness and your Khmer.

Stress, Sleep & Feeling Low

ភាពតានតឹង និងការគេងមិនលក់

Living abroad is tiring in ways that are hard to name. These are the words for saying so.

Friend
មើលទៅអ្នកហត់ណាស់។
meul teuv neak HOT nas.
You look very tired.
You
ខ្ញុំគេងមិនលក់ច្រើនយប់ហើយ។
khnyom keing min LUOK chraen yub haoy.
I haven’t slept well for several nights.
You
ខ្ញុំតានតឹងនឹងការងារ។
khnyom taan-TEUNG neung kaa-ngie.
I’m stressed about work.
Friend
សម្រាកខ្លះទៅ។ ថែរក្សាខ្លួនផង។
som-RAAK khlah teuv. thae-rak-saa kluon phong.
Get some rest. Take care of yourself.
You
ខ្ញុំនឹករលឹកផ្ទះ។
khnyom NEUK ro-leuk phteah.
I’m homesick.
Say It Right

នឹករលឹក (neuk ro-leuk) means “to miss / long for”. Say khnyom neuk ro-leuk phteah and any Cambodian will understand exactly what you mean.

Stress, Sleep & Feeling Low

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
I’m tired.ខ្ញុំហត់khnyom hot
I can’t sleep.ខ្ញុំគេងមិនលក់khnyom keing min luok

I’m homesick.ខ្ញុំនឹករលឹកផ្ទះkhnyom neuk ro-leuk phteah
