Pro-Tip · Feelings Live in the Heart Word

A great many Khmer emotional expressions are built on ចិត្ត (chet), meaning heart or mind: sa-bay chet is happy, min sa-bay chet unhappy, khoeung chet angry, smoh chet sincere. Mental health is rarely discussed openly here and there are few local services, so long-term residents often rely on international clinics in Phnom Penh or on counselling online. Saying you are simply hot — tired — is always understood, and always an acceptable answer.

Ngorn Kakteka126Prepared by Nat Bunchhai
07
Chapter Seven

Work, Business & Study

Job Interview Basics

មូលដ្ឋានគ្រឹះនៃការសម្ភាសន៍

Interviewing a candidate, or being interviewed. Either way these five exchanges carry the meeting.

Manager
សូមណែនាំខ្លួនបន្តិច។
som nae-NOAM kluon bon-tech.
Please introduce yourself.
You
ខ្ញុំមានបទពិសោធន៍ប្រាំឆ្នាំ។
khnyom mien bot-pi-SAOT pram chhnam.
I have five years of experience.
Manager
ហេតុអ្វីចង់ធ្វើការនៅទីនេះ?
haet a-vei chong thveu KAA nov ti-nih?
Why do you want to work here?
You
ខ្ញុំចូលចិត្តការងារជាមួយក្រុម។
khnyom chol-chet kaa-ngie chie-muoy KROM.
I enjoy working with a team.
Manager
តើអ្នកចង់បានប្រាក់ខែប៉ុន្មាន?
tae neak chong baan brak-KHAE pon-man?
What salary are you looking for?
Say It Right

ណែនាំខ្លួន (nae-noam kluon) means “introduce oneself”. The same verb nae-noam is used for recommending a person or a restaurant.

Ngorn Kakteka128Prepared by Nat Bunchhai
Chapter 7 · Work, Business & StudySituation 61
61

Job Interview Basics

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
Interviewការសម្ភាសន៍kaa som-pheas
Please introduce yourself.សូមណែនាំខ្លួនsom nae-noam kluon
Experienceបទពិសោធន៍bot-pi-saot
Salaryប្រាក់ខែbrak-khae
I can start next month.ខ្ញុំអាចចាប់ផ្ដើមខែក្រោយkhnyom ach chap-phdaeum khae kraoy
Full time / part timeពេញម៉ោង / ក្រៅម៉ោងpenh maong / krav maong
Do you speak English?និយាយអង់គ្លេសបានទេ?ni-yiey ong-gleih baan tei?
Thank you for your time.អរគុណសម្រាប់ពេលវេលាor-kun som-rap peil-vei-lie
Pro-Tip · Modesty Reads Better Than Confidence

Western interview style — listing achievements, selling yourself hard — can land badly here, where self-promotion is read as a lack of humility. Cambodian candidates tend to describe what the team accomplished and what they still hope to learn. If you are the one interviewing, note that a quiet candidate is not necessarily an unconfident one; ask what they did rather than how good they are, and you will get a far more accurate answer.

Ngorn Kakteka129Prepared by Nat Bunchhai

Work, Business & Study

Professional Introductions

ការណែនាំក្នុងការងារ

Meeting a client for the first time. Cards are exchanged with two hands, and titles matter.

You
ជម្រាបសួរ លោក។ នេះនាមប័ណ្ណខ្ញុំ។
chom-riep suor, lowk. nih nie-ma-BAN khnyom.
Hello, sir. Here is my business card.
Client
អរគុណ។ អ្នកធ្វើការក្រុមហ៊ុនណា?
or-kun. neak thveu kaa krom-HUN naa?
Thank you. Which company are you with?
You
ខ្ញុំជាអ្នកគ្រប់គ្រងផ្នែកលក់។
khnyom chie neak krop-KRONG phnaek luok.
I’m the sales manager.
Client
រីករាយដែលបានស្គាល់។
rik-RIEY dael baan skoal.
Pleased to meet you.
You
សង្ឃឹមថានឹងសហការគ្នា។
song-KHEUM thaa neung sa-ha-kaa knie.
I hope we can work together.
Say It Right

Give and receive a card with both hands, or with the right hand supported at the elbow by the left. Read it before putting it away — never straight into a back pocket.

Ngorn Kakteka130Prepared by Nat Bunchhai

62

Professional Introductions

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
Companyក្រុមហ៊ុនkrom-hun
Business cardនាមប័ណ្ណnie-ma-ban
Manager / directorអ្នកគ្រប់គ្រង / នាយកneak krop-krong / nie-yok
Colleague / staffសហការី / បុគ្គលិកsa-ha-kaa-rii / bok-ko-lik
I work in the … department.ខ្ញុំធ្វើការផ្នែក …khnyom thveu kaa phnaek …
This is my colleague.នេះជាសហការីខ្ញុំnih chie sa-ha-kaa-rii khnyom
I hope we can work together.សង្ឃឹមថានឹងសហការគ្នាsong-kheum thaa neung sa-ha-kaa knie
May I have your card?សុំនាមប័ណ្ណបានទេ?som nie-ma-ban baan tei?
Pro-Tip · Greet the Most Senior Person First

Cambodian offices are strongly hierarchical, and the order in which you greet a room is noticed by everyone in it. Identify the most senior person — usually the oldest, and the one others defer to — and greet them first, with a sampeah slightly higher than you would use for peers. Use lowk or lowk srei until you are invited to do otherwise, and let them set the tone for how formal the meeting stays.

Ngorn Kakteka131Prepared by Nat Bunchhai

63
Work, Business & Study

In a Meeting

ក្នុងកិច្ចប្រជុំ

Opening, contributing and closing. Disagree gently — the wording here is doing a lot of work.

Chair
សូមចាប់ផ្ដើមប្រជុំ។
som chap-phdaeum bra-CHUM.
Let’s begin the meeting.
You
សុំបញ្ចេញមតិបន្តិចបានទេ?
som banh-chenh MO-TI bon-tech baan tei?
May I share an opinion?
You
ខ្ញុំយល់ស្របជាមួយគំនិតនេះ។
khnyom yul-SROP chie-muoy kum-net nih.
I agree with this idea.
Colleague
ប្រហែលមានវិធីផ្សេងទៀត។
bra-hael mien vi-THII phseng tiet.
Perhaps there’s another way.
Chair
អញ្ចឹងសម្រេចយ៉ាងនេះ។
an-choeng som-RECH yang nih.
Then we’ll decide it this way.
Say It Right

ប្រហែល (bra-hael, “perhaps”) is how Cambodians disagree. “Perhaps there is another way” is a full objection — treat it as one.

Ngorn Kakteka132Prepared by Nat Bunchhai
Chapter 7 · Work, Business & StudySituation 63
63

In a Meeting

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
Meetingកិច្ចប្រជុំkech bra-chum
May I share an opinion?សុំបញ្ចេញមតិបានទេ?som banh-chenh mo-ti baan tei?
I agree.ខ្ញុំយល់ស្របkhnyom yul-srop
Perhaps there’s another way.ប្រហែលមានវិធីផ្សេងទៀតbra-hael mien vi-thii phseng tiet
I don’t quite understand.ខ្ញុំមិនសូវយល់khnyom min sao yul
Could you explain again?ជួយពន្យល់ម្ដងទៀតchuoy pon-yul mdong tiet
Who is responsible for this?អ្នកណាទទួលខុសត្រូវ?neak-naa to-tuol khoh-trov?
When is the deadline?ផុតកំណត់ពេលណា?phot kom-not peil naa?
Pro-Tip · Silence Is Not Agreement

Juniors rarely contradict seniors in front of a room, so a meeting that ends with everyone nodding may have settled nothing at all. The real conversation happens afterwards, one to one. If you are leading, ask people individually and privately, and always finish by asking each person to state back what they will do and by when. Written follow-up in Khmer or simple English prevents the polite nod from becoming a missed deadline.

Ngorn Kakteka133Prepared by Nat Bunchhai

Work, Business & Study

Work Phone Calls

ការទូរស័ព្ទក្នុងការងារ

Answering, taking a message and getting off the line politely — all without seeing the other face.

You
ហាឡូ ក្រុមហ៊ុនអេប៊ីស៊ី សូមស្វាគមន៍។
haa-lou, krom-hun ABC, som svie-KOM.
Hello, ABC Company, good day.
Caller
សុំជួបលោកសុខបានទេ?
som CHUOP lowk Sok baan tei?
May I speak to Mr Sok?
You
គាត់មិននៅទេ។ ចាំបន្តិច។
koat min NOV tei. cham bon-tech.
He isn’t here. One moment.
You
តើអ្នកចង់ផ្ញើសារអ្វីទេ?
tae neak chong PHNHAEU saa a-vei tei?
Would you like to leave a message?
You
ខ្ញុំនឹងឲ្យគាត់ទូរស័ព្ទមកវិញ។
khnyom neung aoy koat tuu-ra-sap mok VINH.
I’ll have him call you back.
Say It Right

គាត់ (koat) is the respectful third-person pronoun for an adult — “he” or “she” alike. Khmer pronouns mark status, not gender.

Ngorn Kakteka134Prepared by Nat Bunchhai
Chapter 7 · Work, Business & StudySituation 64
64

Work Phone Calls

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
Hello (on the phone)ហាឡូhaa-lou
May I speak to …?សុំជួប … បានទេ?som chuop … baan tei?
One moment, please.សូមចាំបន្តិចsom cham bon-tech
He / she isn’t here.គាត់មិននៅទេkoat min nov tei
Leave a messageផ្ញើសារphnhaeu saa
I’ll call you back.ខ្ញុំនឹងទូរស័ព្ទមកវិញkhnyom neung tuu-ra-sap mok vinh
The line is bad.សេវាមិនច្បាស់sei-vie min chbah
Who’s calling, please?សុំទោស នរណាហ្នឹង?som toh, no-naa nung?
Pro-Tip · Business Runs on Telegram

Cambodia does most of its professional messaging on Telegram rather than email — quotes, invoices, contracts and appointments all arrive there, often as photographs of paper documents. Expect voice notes rather than typed replies, and expect to be added to a great many groups. Email is treated as formal and slow; if something is urgent, phone. And answer with your company name, as above: it is what callers expect to hear.

Ngorn Kakteka135Prepared by Nat Bunchhai

65
Work, Business & Study

Messages & Appointments

សារ និងការណាត់ជួប

Fixing a time, confirming it, and rearranging when something inevitably moves.

You
តើយើងណាត់ជួបថ្ងៃណា?
tae yeung NAT chuop thngai naa?
What day shall we meet?
Client
ថ្ងៃពុធ ម៉ោងដប់ព្រឹក បានទេ?
thngai PUT, maong dop pruk, baan tei?
Wednesday at ten, alright?
You
បានហើយ។ ខ្ញុំនឹងផ្ញើសារបញ្ជាក់។
BAAN haoy. khnyom neung phnhaeu saa banh-cheak.
Fine. I’ll send a confirmation message.
You
សុំទោស ខ្ញុំត្រូវពន្យារពេលបន្តិច។
som toh, khnyom trov pon-YIE peil bon-tech.
Sorry, I need to postpone slightly.
Client
អត់អីទេ ប្ដូរទៅថ្ងៃព្រហស្បតិ៍។
ot ei tei, BDO teuv thngai bro-hoah.
No problem, move it to Thursday.
Say It Right

ណាត់ជួប (nat chuop) means “to make an appointment”. បញ្ជាក់ (banh-cheak) means “to confirm” — always do the second after the first.

Ngorn Kakteka136Prepared by Nat Bunchhai
Chapter 7 · Work, Business & StudySituation 65
65

Messages & Appointments

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
Appointmentការណាត់ជួបkaa nat chuop
Monday / Wednesday / Thursdayថ្ងៃច័ន្ទ / ថ្ងៃពុធ / ថ្ងៃព្រហស្បតិ៍thngai chan / put / bro-hoah
Are you free on …?ថ្ងៃ … ទំនេរទេ?thngai … tum-nei tei?
I’ll confirm by message.ខ្ញុំនឹងផ្ញើសារបញ្ជាក់khnyom neung phnhaeu saa banh-cheak
I need to postpone.ខ្ញុំត្រូវពន្យារពេលkhnyom trov pon-yie peil
I’ll be a little late.ខ្ញុំនឹងយឺតបន្តិចkhnyom neung yoeut bon-tech
Please send me the documents.សូមផ្ញើឯកសារមកខ្ញុំsom phnhaeu aek-ka-saa mok khnyom
I’ve received it, thank you.ខ្ញុំទទួលបានហើយkhnyom to-tuol baan haoy
Pro-Tip · Confirm the Morning Of

An appointment agreed a week ahead is an intention, not a commitment; traffic, rain, family obligations and more senior people all outrank it. Send a short confirming message on the morning of the meeting — this is normal practice, not nagging, and it is how Cambodians manage their own diaries. Build slack into your day, and treat a cancellation as circumstance rather than rudeness.

Ngorn Kakteka137Prepared by Nat Bunchhai
Chapter 7 · Work, Business & StudySituation 66
66
Work, Business & Study

Small Talk at Work

ការនិយាយលេងជាមួយសហការី

The lunch hour is where working relationships are actually built. Join in.

Colleague
ថ្ងៃនេះរវល់ណាស់មែនទេ?
thngai nih ro-VOL nas maen tei?
Busy day today, isn’t it?
You
មែនហើយ! ការងារច្រើនណាស់។
maen haoy! kaa-ngie CHRAEN nas.
Yes! So much work.
Colleague
ទៅញ៉ាំបាយជាមួយគ្នាទេ?
teuv nyam bay chie-muoy KNIE tei?
Shall we go for lunch together?
You
បាទ ទៅ! ថ្ងៃចុងសប្ដាហ៍ធ្វើអ្វី?
baat, TEUV! thngai chong sap-daa thveu a-vei?
Yes, let’s! What are you doing at the weekend?
Colleague
ត្រឡប់ទៅស្រុកកំណើត។
tro-LOP teuv srok kom-naeut.
Going back to my home province.
Say It Right

ស្រុកកំណើត (srok kom-naeut) is “home village / birthplace”. Almost everyone working in Phnom Penh has one, and asking about it is a warm, safe question.

Ngorn Kakteka138Prepared by Nat Bunchhai
Chapter 7 · Work, Business & StudySituation 66
66

Small Talk at Work

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
Busy today, isn’t it?ថ្ងៃនេះរវល់ណាស់មែនទេ?thngai nih ro-vol nas maen tei?
Shall we eat together?ទៅញ៉ាំបាយជាមួយគ្នាទេ?teuv nyam bay chie-muoy knie tei?
The weekendថ្ងៃចុងសប្ដាហ៍thngai chong sap-daa
Home province / villageស្រុកកំណើតsrok kom-naeut
How long have you worked here?ធ្វើការនៅទីនេះបានប៉ុន្មានហើយ?thveu kaa nov ti-nih baan pon-man haoy?
Have a good weekend.សូមរីករាយថ្ងៃឈប់សម្រាកsom rik-riey thngai chhup som-raak
See you tomorrow.ជួបគ្នាថ្ងៃស្អែកchuop knie thngai sa-aek
I’m going home now.ខ្ញុំត្រឡប់ទៅផ្ទះហើយkhnyom tro-lop teuv phteah haoy
Pro-Tip · Eat Lunch With the Team

Lunch in a Cambodian office is a shared, communal affair, often eaten together at someone’s desk or at the same stall every day. Turning it down repeatedly to work through — a virtue in some workplaces — reads here as keeping yourself apart. Say yes, pay your share, ask about people’s families and home provinces, and the working relationship that follows will be far more open than any number of meetings could produce.

Ngorn Kakteka139Prepared by Nat Bunchhai
Chapter 7 · Work, Business & StudySituation 67
67
Work, Business & Study

Instructing Staff

ការណែនាំបុគ្គលិក

Giving clear instructions and correcting mistakes without causing anyone to lose face.

You
ជួយរៀបចំរបាយការណ៍នេះផង។
chuoy riep-CHOM ro-bay-kaa nih phong.
Please prepare this report.
Staff
បាទ ត្រូវការពេលណា?
baat, trov-kaa PEIL naa?
Yes, when do you need it?
You
មុនម៉ោងបួនរសៀល។
mun maong BUON ro-siel.
Before four in the afternoon.
You
ត្រង់នេះខុសបន្តិច ជួយកែផង។
trong nih KHOH bon-tech, chuoy kae phong.
This part is slightly wrong, please fix it.
You
ធ្វើបានល្អណាស់ អរគុណ។
thveu baan LA-OR nas, or-kun.
Very well done, thank you.
Say It Right

Frame instructions as requests: chuoy … phong means “please help … ”. A bare command is grammatically fine and socially cold; the chuoy … phong wrapper costs two words.

Ngorn Kakteka140Prepared by Nat Bunchhai
Chapter 7 · Work, Business & StudySituation 67
67

Instructing Staff

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
Please help me … (request)ជួយ … ផងchuoy … phong
When do you need it?ត្រូវការពេលណា?trov-kaa peil naa?
Before four o’clockមុនម៉ោងបួនmun maong buon
This part is wrong.ត្រង់នេះខុសtrong nih khoh
Please fix it.ជួយកែផងchuoy kae phong
Do you understand?យល់ទេ?yul tei?
Very well done.ធ្វើបានល្អណាស់thveu baan la-or nas
Take your time.មិនបាច់ប្រញាប់ទេmin bach bra-nhap tei
Pro-Tip · Correct in Private, Praise in Public

Criticising someone in front of colleagues causes a loss of face that can quietly end their willingness to work with you, and they will rarely tell you so. Correct quietly, one to one, and soften it — khoh bon-tech, “slightly wrong”, does the job. Praise, by contrast, should be given openly. And never ask yul tei? expecting a truthful no; ask instead for the task to be explained back to you.

Ngorn Kakteka141Prepared by Nat Bunchhai
Chapter 7 · Work, Business & StudySituation 68
68
Work, Business & Study

Negotiating a Contract

ការចរចាកិច្ចសន្យា

Agreeing terms for a service. Get the price, the deadline and the payment schedule in writing.

You
តម្លៃសរុបប៉ុន្មាន?
tom-lai sa-ROP pon-man?
What is the total price?
Supplier
ពីរពាន់ដុល្លារ រួមទាំងដំឡើង។
pii poan dol-laa, ruom teang dom-LAEUNG.
Two thousand dollars, installation included.
You
បង់មុនប៉ុន្មានភាគរយ?
bong mun pon-man phiek-ROY?
What percentage is paid up front?
Supplier
សាមសិបភាគរយ នៅសល់ពេលរួចរាល់។
saam-sep phiek-roy, nov SOL peil ruoch-roal.
Thirty per cent, the rest on completion.
You
សូមសរសេរក្នុងកិច្ចសន្យា។
som sor-sei knong kech-son-YIE.
Please put that in the contract.
Say It Right

រួមទាំង (ruom teang) means “including”; មិនរាប់ (min roab) means “not including”. Ask which applies to every line of a quotation.

Ngorn Kakteka142Prepared by Nat Bunchhai

Negotiating a Contract

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
Contractកិច្ចសន្យាkech-son-yie
What is the total price?តម្លៃសរុបប៉ុន្មាន?tom-lai sa-rop pon-man?
Including / not includingរួមទាំង / មិនរាប់ruom teang / min roab
Deposit / balanceប្រាក់កក់ / ប្រាក់នៅសល់brak kok / brak nov sol
When will it be finished?រួចរាល់ពេលណា?ruoch-roal peil naa?
Please put it in writing.សូមសរសេរជាលាយលក្ខណ៍អក្សរsom sor-sei chie lie-lak ak-so

Is there a guarantee?មានធានាទេ?mien thie-nie tei?
Pro-Tip · Bilingual, and Two Copies

Have any contract that matters drawn up in Khmer and English side by side, with both parties signing every page and each keeping an original. Where the two versions differ, the Khmer text is what a Cambodian court will read — so pay a local lawyer to check it rather than relying on a translation you cannot verify. Stage the payments against delivered work; a deposit of thirty per cent is normal, paying everything up front is not.

In the Language Class

ក្នុងថ្នាក់រៀនភាសា

The classroom phrases that let you learn faster — and that work in any lesson, on any subject.

Teacher
ថ្ងៃនេះយើងរៀនមេរៀនទីប្រាំ។
thngai nih yeung rien mei-rien ti PRAM.
Today we study lesson five.
You
លោកគ្រូ សុំសួរបន្តិចបានទេ?
lowk KRUU, som suo bon-tech baan tei?
Teacher, may I ask something?
You
ពាក្យនេះអានយ៉ាងម៉េច?
peak nih AAN yang mech?
How is this word pronounced?
Teacher
ល្អណាស់! ធ្វើលំហាត់ផ្ទះទំព័រដប់។
LA-OR nas! thveu lom-hat phteah tum-po dop.
Very good! Do the homework on page ten.
You
សុំមេរៀនម្ដងទៀតបានទេ?
som mei-RIEN mdong tiet baan tei?
Could we go over it once more?
Say It Right

Address a male teacher as លោកគ្រូ (lowk kruu) and a female one as អ្នកគ្រូ (neak kruu). Teachers are held in genuinely high regard in Cambodia.

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics

Student / lessonសិស្ស / មេរៀនseh / mei-rien

Pro-Tip · Learn the Alphabet Early

Romanisation gets you speaking in week one — that is what this book is for — but it will quietly cap your progress, because no two systems agree and none captures Khmer vowels exactly. The script has 33 consonants and two vowel series, and most learners can read simple signs after a few weeks of steady work. Start with the consonants you meet daily on shopfronts, and treat every ផ្សារ and វត្ត you pass as a free flashcard.

Work, Business & Study

Talking About Your Job

ការនិយាយអំពីការងាររបស់អ្នក

You will be asked what you do and what you earn. Here is how to answer both — one fully, one lightly.

Neighbour
តើអ្នកធ្វើការអ្វី?
tae neak thveu KAA a-vei?
What work do you do?
You
ខ្ញុំធ្វើការនៅអង្គការមួយ។
khnyom thveu kaa nov ong-KAA muoy.
I work for an organisation.
Neighbour
ប្រាក់ខែច្រើនទេ?
brak-khae CHRAEN tei?
Is the salary good?
You
គ្រប់គ្រាន់ហើយ អរគុណ។
krop-KROAN haoy, or-kun.
It’s enough, thank you.
You
ខ្ញុំចូលចិត្តការងារនេះណាស់។
khnyom chol-CHET kaa-ngie nih nas.
I like this job very much.
Say It Right

គ្រប់គ្រាន់ហើយ (krop-kroan haoy) — “it’s enough” — is the perfect answer to a salary question. It is honest, modest, and closes the subject warmly.

Ngorn Kakteka146Prepared by Nat Bunchhai

Teacher / doctor / engineerគ្រូ / គ្រូពេទ្យ / វិស្វករkruu / kruu-peit / vih-va-ko
Businessperson / studentអ្នកជំនួញ / និស្សិតneak chum-nuonh / ni-set

Pro-Tip · The Salary Question Is Not Rude

Asking what you earn, what your rent is or what your motorbike cost is ordinary friendly curiosity here, not an intrusion — Cambodians ask each other the same things freely. You are not obliged to answer with a number, and krop-kroan haoy handles it gracefully. Bear in mind that a foreign salary is often many times a local one, so a precise figure can quietly change a friendship; vagueness is kinder to everybody.

Social Life & Relationships

Making Plans

ការរៀបចំកម្មវិធី

Fixing a time with a friend. Keep it loose — plans here are made and remade all day.

You
ថ្ងៃសៅរ៍អ្នកទំនេរទេ?
thngai SAO neak tum-nei tei?
Are you free on Saturday?
Friend
ទំនេរ។ ចង់ទៅណា?
tum-NEI. chong teuv naa?
Yes. Where do you want to go?
You
ទៅញ៉ាំបាយមាត់ទន្លេទេ?
teuv nyam bay MOAT ton-lei tei?
Shall we eat by the river?
Friend
បាទ! ជួបគ្នាម៉ោងប្រាំមួយ។
baat! chuop knie maong PRAM-muoy.
Yes! Let’s meet at six.
You
ខ្ញុំនឹងផ្ញើសារបញ្ជាក់។
khnyom neung phnhaeu saa banh-CHEAK.
I’ll message to confirm.
Say It Right

ទំនេរ (tum-nei) means “free / unoccupied” and works for people, tables and taxis alike. tum-nei tei? is a complete question on its own.

Ngorn Kakteka149Prepared by Nat Bunchhai
Chapter 8 · Social Life & RelationshipsSituation 71
71

Making Plans

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
Are you free?អ្នកទំនេរទេ?neak tum-nei tei?
Saturday / Sundayថ្ងៃសៅរ៍ / ថ្ងៃអាទិត្យthngai sao / thngai aa-tit

What time suits you?ម៉ោងណាស្រួលសម្រាប់អ្នក?maong naa sruol som-rap neak?
I’m busy that day.ថ្ងៃនោះខ្ញុំរវល់thngai nuh khnyom ro-vol

Pro-Tip · Plans Breathe

A Cambodian “yes” to a social plan means yes, in principle. Rain, a family obligation or a request from someone senior will move it without much ceremony, and this is not considered flaky — the relationship matters more than the calendar. Confirm on the day, arrive expecting a flexible start, and do the same yourself without guilt. Friendships here are maintained by frequent small contact rather than by punctual appointments.

Ngorn Kakteka150Prepared by Nat Bunchhai

Social Life & Relationships

Inviting Someone Out

ការអញ្ជើញនរណាម្នាក់

Extending an invitation, and settling the question of who pays before it becomes awkward.

You
ខ្ញុំចង់អញ្ជើញអ្នកញ៉ាំបាយ។
khnyom chong an-CHOEUN neak nyam bay.
I’d like to invite you for a meal.
Friend
អរគុណ! នៅហាងណា?
or-kun! nov HANG naa?
Thank you! Which restaurant?
You
ហាងជិតផ្សារ។ ខ្ញុំរៀបចំឲ្យ។
hang CHIT phsaa. khnyom riep-chom aoy.
The place near the market. I’ll arrange it.
Friend
យើងចែកគ្នាបង់ទេ?
yeung CHAEK knie bong tei?
Shall we split the bill?
You
ថ្ងៃនេះខ្ញុំរៀបចំ។ លើកក្រោយអ្នក។
thngai nih khnyom RIEP-CHOM. leuk kraoy neak.
Today it’s on me. Next time, you.
Say It Right

អញ្ជើញ (an-choeun) is both “to invite” and “please, go ahead”. Whoever says khnyom an-choeun is usually understood to be paying.

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics

Would you like to come?ចង់ទៅជាមួយគ្នាទេ?chong teuv chie-muoy knie tei?
For coffee / for a mealផឹកកាហ្វេ / ញ៉ាំបាយpheuk kaa-fei / nyam bay

Pro-Tip · The Inviter Pays

Splitting a bill item by item is uncommon here. Whoever proposed the outing generally settles it, and the balance is restored next time rather than on the night — which is exactly what leuk kraoy neak means. Bear in mind the income gap: insisting a Cambodian friend on a local salary pay half of a foreigner-priced dinner puts them in a difficult position they will never mention. Pay, lightly, and let them host you somewhere of their choosing later.

Ngorn Kakteka152Prepared by Nat Bunchhai

Social Life & Relationships

Parties & Weddings

ជប់លៀង និងអាពាហ៍ពិពាហ៍

You have been handed a wedding invitation by a colleague. Accept — and bring an envelope.

Colleague
ខ្ញុំរៀបការថ្ងៃទីដប់។ អញ្ជើញមក!
khnyom riep-KAA thngai ti dop. an-choeun mok!
I’m getting married on the tenth. Please come!
You
អបអរសាទរ! ខ្ញុំនឹងទៅ។
ap-or-saa-TO! khnyom neung teuv.
Congratulations! I’ll be there.
You
កម្មវិធីចាប់ផ្ដើមម៉ោងប៉ុន្មាន?
kam-ma-vi-thii chap-phdaeum MAONG pon-man?
What time does it start?
Colleague
ល្ងាចម៉ោងប្រាំ នៅឯវត្ត។
lngiech maong PRAM, nov ae voat.
Five in the evening, at the pagoda.
You
សូមជូនពរឲ្យមានសុភមង្គល។
som choun PO aoy mien so-phak-mong-kol.
I wish you every happiness.
Say It Right

អបអរសាទរ (ap-or-saa-to) is “congratulations”, used for weddings, graduations and new babies alike. Four syllables, evenly stressed.

Parties & Weddings

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
Weddingអាពាហ៍ពិពាហ៍aa-peah pi-peah
Party / celebrationជប់លៀងchob-lieng
Congratulations!អបអរសាទរ!ap-or-saa-to!
I’m getting married.ខ្ញុំរៀបការkhnyom riep-kaa

Pro-Tip · Money in an Envelope

Cambodian weddings are enormous — several hundred guests are ordinary — and the gift is cash in the envelope that came with your invitation, handed in at a table by the door where it is recorded in a book. Twenty to fifty dollars is a normal range depending on how close you are. Dress smartly and brightly; black alone is for funerals. Arriving an hour after the printed time is completely standard, and you may find the party still filling up.

Ngorn Kakteka154Prepared by Nat Bunchhai

Compliments

ការសរសើរ

Praising a person, a home, a meal or a language attempt. Compliments are warmly received here.

You
អាវនេះស្អាតណាស់!
aav nih S-AT nas!
That shirt is lovely!
Friend
អរគុណ! ទើបទិញថ្មី។
or-kun! teub tinh THMEI.
Thank you! I just bought it.
Friend
អ្នកនិយាយខ្មែរពិរោះណាស់!
neak ni-yiey khmae PI-ROH nas!
You speak Khmer beautifully!
You
អត់ទេ ខ្ញុំនៅរៀនតិចតួច។
ot tei, khnyom nov rien TECH-tuoch.
Not at all, I’m still learning a little.
You
ផ្ទះអ្នកស្អាតណាស់។
phteah neak S-AT nas.
Your home is beautiful.
Say It Right

ស្អាត (s-at) means both “beautiful” and “clean”. Said of a house it is high praise; said of a person it means good-looking.

Ngorn Kakteka155Prepared by Nat Bunchhai
Chapter 8 · Social Life & RelationshipsSituation 74
74

Compliments

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
Beautiful / lovelyស្អាតs-at
Handsomeសង្ហាsong-haa
You speak Khmer well.អ្នកនិយាយខ្មែរពិរោះណាស់neak ni-yiey khmae pi-roh nas
You’re very kind.អ្នកចិត្តល្អណាស់neak chet la-or nas
Your home is lovely.ផ្ទះអ្នកស្អាតណាស់phteah neak s-at nas
Clever / capableពូកែpu-kae
Not at all. (deflecting)អត់ទេot tei
You’re too kind.អ្នកសរសើរពេកneak sor-saeu peik
Pro-Tip · Deflect, Don’t Accept

Receiving praise with a straight “thank you” can sound like agreement, and agreement sounds like pride. Cambodians deflect first — ot tei, “not at all” — and then thank. Do the same when your Khmer is complimented, which will happen constantly and often generously. Keep compliments to appearance, clothes, home and cooking; comments on a person’s body or weight, normal between close Cambodian friends, are best avoided by a newcomer.

Ngorn Kakteka156Prepared by Nat Bunchhai

Social Life & Relationships

Talking About Family

ការនិយាយអំពីគ្រួសារ

Family is the first subject anyone will ask about, and the one they most want to hear about.

Friend
តើអ្នករៀបការហើយឬនៅ?
tae neak riep-KAA haoy reu nov?
Are you married yet?
You
រៀបការហើយ មានកូនពីរនាក់។
riep-KAA haoy, mien koun pii neak.
Yes, I have two children.
Friend
ពួកគេនៅជាមួយអ្នកទេ?
puok-kei nov chie-muoy NEAK tei?
Are they here with you?
You
អត់ទេ គេនៅស្រុកខ្ញុំ។
ot tei, kei nov SROK khnyom.
No, they’re in my country.
You
ចុះអ្នកវិញ? មានបងប្អូនប៉ុន្មាននាក់?
choh neak vinh? mien bong-P’OUN pon-man neak?
And you? How many brothers and sisters?
Say It Right

បងប្អូន (bong-p’oun) literally means “elder-younger” and covers all siblings at once. Khmer marks relative age before it marks gender.

Ngorn Kakteka157Prepared by Nat Bunchhai
Chapter 8 · Social Life & RelationshipsSituation 75
75

Talking About Family

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
Familyគ្រួសារkruo-saa
Father / motherឪពុក / ម្ដាយov-puk / mdaay
Husband / wifeប្ដី / ប្រពន្ធbdei / bra-pon

Are you married?រៀបការហើយឬនៅ?riep-kaa haoy reu nov?

Pro-Tip · The Family Is the Unit

Cambodian identity is rooted in family far more than in the individual, and much of a young worker’s salary goes home to parents in the province every month. Asking after someone’s parents and children is the warmest thing you can do; describing your own family — even briefly, even in poor Khmer — moves you from foreigner to person. If you are over thirty and unmarried, expect kind bewilderment and possibly an introduction.

Visiting Someone’s Home

ការទៅលេងផ្ទះគេ

Arriving at a family house. Shoes off at the door, greet the eldest, and accept the drink.

Host
អញ្ជើញចូល! អញ្ជើញអង្គុយ។
an-choeun CHOUL! an-choeun ong-kuy.
Please come in! Please sit down.
You
អរគុណ។ ដោះស្បែកជើងទេ?
or-kun. DOH sbaek-choeung tei?

Host
បាទ ដោះនៅមុខទ្វារ។ ផឹកទឹកទេ?
baat, doh nov muk tvie. PHEUK tuk tei?

You
សុំទឹកមួយកែវ អរគុណ។
som tuk muoy KAEV, or-kun.

ផ្ទះអ្នកកក់ក្ដៅណាស់។
phteah neak kok-KDAV nas.
Your home is very welcoming.

កក់ក្ដៅ (kok-kdav) literally means “warm”, but of a home it means welcoming and full of affection — a compliment any host is pleased to hear.

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics

Pro-Tip · Shoes Off, Head Down, Feet Away

Three rules cover most of home etiquette. Take your shoes off at the door, always. Lower your head slightly when passing in front of someone seated and older. And never point the soles of your feet at a person or at the household shrine — sit cross-legged or with your feet tucked behind you. The head is the most sacred part of the body and the feet the least, which is why patting even a child’s head is best avoided.

Giving & Receiving Gifts

ការជូន និងទទួលអំណោយ

Handing over a small gift. Two hands, a modest word, and no expectation that it is opened.

You
នេះជាអំណោយតូចមួយសម្រាប់អ្នក។
nih chie om-NAOY touch muoy som-rap neak.
This is a small gift for you.
Friend
អូ! មិនបាច់ទេ អរគុណច្រើន!
ouh! min BACH tei, or-kun chraen!
Oh! You shouldn’t have, thank you!
You
របស់តូចតាចទេ។
ro-boh TOUCH-taach tei.
It’s only a little thing.
Friend
អ្នកគិតដល់ខ្ញុំណាស់។
neak KET dol khnyom nas.
That’s very thoughtful of you.
You
សូមទទួលដោយក្ដីរីករាយ។
som to-tuol daoy kdei rik-RIEY.
Please accept it with pleasure.
Say It Right

ជូន (choun) is the polite verb “to give” — used upwards, to elders and guests. The plain verb ឲ្យ (aoy) is for everyday giving.

Giving & Receiving Gifts

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics

Pro-Tip · Give With Two Hands, Don’t Expect It Opened

Offer and receive gifts with both hands, and do not be surprised when yours is set aside unopened — opening a present in front of the giver can seem greedy, so it is enjoyed privately later. Fruit, cakes and useful household things travel well; avoid anything sharp, and avoid white wrapping or white flowers, which belong to funerals. When visiting a family home, a bag of fruit for the household is always the right answer.

Apologising Properly

ការសុំទោសឲ្យបានត្រឹមត្រូវ

Something went wrong and it was your fault. Say so plainly — it repairs faster than explaining.

You
សូមអភ័យទោស ខ្ញុំមកយឺត។
som a-PHEY toh, khnyom mok yoeut.
I sincerely apologise for being late.
Friend
អត់អីទេ ខ្ញុំក៏ទើបមកដែរ។
ot ei tei, khnyom kâ TEUB mok dae.
It’s fine, I just arrived too.
You
ខ្ញុំយល់ច្រឡំ។ កំហុសខ្ញុំ។
khnyom yul chro-LOM. kom-hoh khnyom.
I misunderstood. It was my mistake.
You
ខ្ញុំមិនចង់ធ្វើឲ្យអ្នកខឹងទេ។
khnyom min chong thveu aoy neak KHEUNG tei.
I didn’t mean to upset you.
Friend
ភ្លេចវាទៅ។ យើងនៅជាមិត្ត។
PHLECH vie teuv. yeung nov chie mit.
Forget it. We’re still friends.
Say It Right

សូមអភ័យទោស (som a-phey toh) is the full, formal apology; សូមទោស (som toh) is the everyday one. Use the long form when it genuinely matters.

Apologising Properly

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
I sincerely apologise.សូមអភ័យទោសsom a-phey toh
It was my mistake.កំហុសខ្ញុំkom-hoh khnyom

Are you angry with me?អ្នកខឹងខ្ញុំទេ?neak kheung khnyom tei?

Pro-Tip · Anger Costs More Than the Problem

Losing your temper in public is remembered long after whatever caused it is forgotten, and it can permanently damage a working or personal relationship. A person who has been shouted at will usually keep smiling — and quietly withdraw. Apologise early, apologise simply, and do not pile on explanations, which read as excuses. A calm kom-hoh khnyom and a small gift the next day repairs almost anything.

Ngorn Kakteka164Prepared by Nat Bunchhai

Saying No Politely

ការបដិសេធដោយសុភាព

Declining an invitation, a price, or a persistent seller — without hardness and without lying.

Seller
ទិញមួយទៅ បង! ថោកណាស់។
tinh muoy teuv, bong! THAOK nas.
Buy one! It’s very cheap.
You
អរគុណ តែខ្ញុំមិនត្រូវការទេ។
or-kun, tae khnyom min TROV-KAA tei.
Thank you, but I don’t need it.
Friend
ល្ងាចនេះទៅជប់លៀងជាមួយគ្នាទេ?
lngiech nih teuv chob-LIENG chie-muoy knie tei?
Coming to the party tonight?
You
សុំទោស ថ្ងៃនេះខ្ញុំមិនអាចទេ។
som toh, thngai nih khnyom min ACH tei.
Sorry, I can’t today.
You
លើកក្រោយប្រាកដជាទៅ។
LEUK kraoy bra-kot chie teuv.

Say It Right

Soften every refusal with or-kun in front and an offer of leuk kraoy — “next time” — behind. A bare ot tei is not wrong, just cold.

Saying No Politely

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics

I’m sorry, I’m busy.សុំទោស ខ្ញុំរវល់som toh, khnyom ro-vol

Pro-Tip · The Smile-and-Keep-Walking

With persistent street sellers, the effective response is not a firmer no but a softer one delivered while still moving: a smile, ot tei, or-kun, and a small wave without breaking stride. Stopping to explain invites a longer negotiation. Note too that Cambodians rarely refuse outright, so if you hear bra-hael or cham meul sen — “let me see” — from someone, that is very often a polite no.

Pro-Tip · Telegram Is the Address Book

Phone numbers here are held on Telegram rather than in email or on paper, and it is where friends, landlords, drivers, colleagues and shops all reach you. Expect voice messages instead of typed ones — recording a reply is faster than typing Khmer script, and it is excellent listening practice for you. Sending chom-riep suor kruo-saa chum-nuoh khnyom, “say hello to your family for me”, is a small courtesy that lands very warmly.

Buying a pass at the ticket office outside Siem Reap. Decide how many days before you queue.

You

som som-bot BEI thngai muoy.

ប្រាំមួយសិបពីរដុល្លារ។ សុំថតរូប។

Pro-Tip · Cover Your Shoulders and Knees

Angkor is a working sacred site, not only a ruin, and the dress code is enforced at the upper level of Angkor Wat: shoulders and knees covered for everyone. Carry a scarf. Go at sunrise for Angkor Wat and late afternoon for Ta Prohm and Bayon, avoiding the coach hours in between. Children selling postcards at the gates should be politely declined — buying encourages families to keep them out of school.

What is the story of this?នេះមានរឿងអ្វី?nih mien roeung a-vei?
Can we rest a moment?សម្រាកបន្តិចបានទេ?som-raak bon-tech baan tei?
Thank you, that was excellent.អរគុណ ល្អណាស់or-kun, la-or nas
Pro-Tip · Ask to See the Licence

Official Angkor guides carry a photo licence badge and have passed real examinations in history and languages; unlicensed guides are cheaper and often far less informed. Book through your guesthouse or the tourism office. A tip of five to ten dollars at the end of a full day is normal and genuinely appreciated, and a guide who has been treated well will happily take you to the quieter temples nobody else visits.

Ngorn Kakteka173Prepared by Nat Bunchhai

83
Travel, Culture & Leisure

At the Pagoda

នៅវត្ត

Visiting a working monastery. Speak quietly, sit low, and know the words for respect.

You
ចូលទៅក្នុងវិហារបានទេ?
CHOUL teuv knong vi-hie baan tei?
May I go into the temple hall?
Layman
បាន តែដោះស្បែកជើងសិន។
baan, tae DOH sbaek-choeung sen.
Yes, but take off your shoes first.
You
ថតរូបបានទេ?
THOT ruup baan tei?
May I take photographs?
Layman
បាន តែកុំថតព្រះសង្ឃ។
baan, tae kom thot preah SONG.
Yes, but not the monks.
You
ខ្ញុំសូមថ្វាយបង្គំព្រះ។
khnyom som thvay bong-KOM preah.
I would like to pay my respects.
Say It Right

ព្រះ (preah) marks anything sacred — the Buddha, monks, kings. ព្រះសង្ឃ (preah song) is a monk, and the word is always said with care.

83

At the Pagoda

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics

Monkព្រះសង្ឃpreah song

Pro-Tip · Women Do Not Touch Monks

A monk may not be touched by a woman, nor accept anything directly from her hand — objects are set down on a cloth for him to pick up. This is not a slight; it is monastic discipline, and Cambodian women observe it automatically. Everyone should sit lower than a monk, keep their feet pointed away, and dress with shoulders and knees covered. A donation box at the door is the right place for money.

Ngorn Kakteka175Prepared by Nat Bunchhai

Travel, Culture & Leisure

Holidays & Festivals

ពិធីបុណ្យ និងថ្ងៃឈប់សម្រាក

Three festivals shut the country down. Knowing which is coming saves a great deal of confusion.

Colleague
អាទិត្យក្រោយចូលឆ្នាំខ្មែរ។
aa-tit kraoy choul chhnam KHMAE.
Next week is Khmer New Year.
You
ឈប់សម្រាកប៉ុន្មានថ្ងៃ?
chhup som-raak pon-man THNGAI?
How many days is the holiday?
Colleague
បីថ្ងៃ។ ខ្ញុំត្រឡប់ទៅស្រុក។
bei thngai. khnyom tro-lop teuv SROK.
Three days. I’m going back to my province.
You
សូមអោយបុណ្យសប្បាយ!
som aoy BON sa-bay!
Have a happy festival!
You
តើគេធ្វើអ្វីខ្លះក្នុងបុណ្យនេះ?
tae kei thveu a-vei KHLAH knong bon nih?
What do people do at this festival?
Say It Right

បុណ្យ (bon) means both “festival” and “merit”. thveu bon — “to make merit” — is what the festivals are for.

Ngorn Kakteka176Prepared by Nat Bunchhai
Chapter 9 · Travel, Culture & LeisureSituation 84
84

Holidays & Festivals

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
Festivalបុណ្យbon
Khmer New Yearចូលឆ្នាំខ្មែរchoul chhnam khmae
Pchum Ben (ancestors)ភ្ជុំបិណ្ឌpchum ben
Water Festivalបុណ្យអុំទូកbon om touk
How many days off?ឈប់សម្រាកប៉ុន្មានថ្ងៃ?chhup som-raak pon-man thngai?
Happy festival!សូមអោយបុណ្យសប្បាយ!som aoy bon sa-bay!

Pro-Tip · Plan Around the Big Three

Khmer New Year in mid-April empties the cities entirely as everyone returns to their home village; expect water thrown in the streets and almost nothing open for a week. Pchum Ben in September or October is for feeding the ancestors at the pagoda, and is quieter and more solemn. Bon Om Touk in November fills Phnom Penh’s riverside with boat races and enormous crowds. Book transport weeks ahead, or do not travel at all.

Travel, Culture & Leisure

At the Beach

នៅឆ្នេរសមុទ្រ

Renting a chair, ordering a crab, and checking whether it is safe to swim today.

You
ជួលកៅអីមួយថ្ងៃប៉ុន្មាន?
chuol KAV-EI muoy thngai pon-man?
How much to rent a chair for the day?
Vendor
មួយដុល្លារ បើទិញម្ហូបគឺឥតគិតថ្លៃ។
muoy dol-laa; baeu tinh mhoub keu ET ket thlai.
One dollar, free if you buy food.
You
សុំក្ដាមអាំងមួយចាន។
som KDAAM ang muoy chaan.
One plate of grilled crab, please.
You
ថ្ងៃនេះហែលទឹកបានទេ?
thngai nih HAEL tuk baan tei?
Is it safe to swim today?
Vendor
បាន តែរលកខ្លាំងបន្តិច។
baan, tae ro-LOK khlang bon-tech.
Yes, but the waves are a bit strong.
Say It Right

ហែលទឹក (hael tuk) is “to swim”, literally “swim water”. The sea is សមុទ្រ (sa-mot); a river is ទន្លេ (ton-lei).

At the Beach

Phrases

Key Phrases

Pro-Tip · Cambodians Swim Dressed

On local beaches you will notice Cambodian women swimming fully clothed — shirt, shorts, sometimes a hat. Bikinis are normal on tourist beaches at Otres or on the islands, and quietly out of place at a family beach in Kep or Kampot. Sun and sea are stronger than they look; the sun is directly overhead at midday and the currents around the islands are real. Ask hael tuk baan tei? before going in.

Travel, Culture & Leisure

Countryside & Villages

ជនបទ និងភូមិ

Out among the rice fields. Village Khmer is slower and warmer, and everyone will want to talk.

Farmer
មកពីណា បង? វង្វេងទេ?
mok pii NAA, bong? vong-veng tei?
Where are you from? Are you lost?
You
អត់ទេ ខ្ញុំមកលេងភូមិ។
ot tei, khnyom mok leing PHUM.
No, I’ve come to visit the village.
You
ស្រែនេះស្អាតណាស់។ ដាំស្រូវអីខ្លះ?
SRAE nih s-at nas. dam srov ei khlah?
These fields are beautiful. What rice do you grow?
Farmer
ស្រូវក្រអូប។ អញ្ជើញផឹកទឹកដូង។
srov kro-OB. an-choeun pheuk tuk-doung.
Fragrant rice. Come and have a coconut.
You
អរគុណច្រើន បង!
or-KUN chraen, bong!
Thank you very much!
Say It Right

ស្រែ (srae) is a rice field; ស្រូវ (srov) is rice growing in it; បាយ (bay) is cooked rice on your plate. Three words, one crop.

Phrases

Key Phrases

Pro-Tip · Accept the Coconut

Rural hospitality is offered immediately and generously, often by people with very little, and refusing it politely still reads as refusal. Accept the drink or the fruit, sit down for ten minutes, and answer the questions about where you are from — that is the exchange. Never photograph inside a house or of children without asking. And in remote areas near the Thai border, stay on marked paths: unexploded ordnance is still a genuine hazard.

Asking to Take Photos

ការសុំអនុញ្ញាតថតរូប

Six words that turn a stolen photograph into a shared one — and often into a conversation.

You
សុំថតរូបបានទេ?
som THOT ruup baan tei?
May I take a photo?
Seller
បាន! ថតទៅ។
BAAN! thot teuv.
Yes! Go ahead.
You
សុំថតជាមួយគ្នាបានទេ?
som thot chie-muoy KNIE baan tei?
May I take one together with you?
You
ខ្ញុំនឹងផ្ញើរូបទៅឲ្យ។
khnyom neung phnhaeu RUUP teuv aoy.
I’ll send you the picture.
Seller
អរគុណ! សុំលេខទូរស័ព្ទ។
or-kun! som LEIK tuu-ra-sap.
Thank you! Give me your number.
Say It Right

ថតរូប (thot ruup) is “to take a photo”. Add chie-muoy knie — “together” — and you have asked for a picture with someone rather than of them.

Asking to Take Photos

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics

Pro-Tip · Ask, Then Actually Send It

Asking first is the difference between a tourist and a guest, and the answer is nearly always a delighted yes. Then keep the promise: take the person’s Telegram number and send the photograph. Many Cambodians have few good pictures of themselves, and a printed copy delivered on a second visit is a gift people remember for years. Never photograph monks without permission, nor children without a parent’s.

Cinema & Karaoke

រោងកុន និងខារ៉ាអូខេ

A night out. Karaoke is the national pastime, and you will be handed the microphone.

You
សុំសំបុត្រកុនពីរ។
som som-bot KON pii.
Two cinema tickets, please.
Clerk
កុនចាប់ផ្ដើមម៉ោងប្រាំពីរ។
kon chap-phdaeum maong PRAM-pil.
The film starts at seven.
Friend
ក្រោយកុន ទៅច្រៀងខារ៉ាអូខេទេ?
kraoy kon, teuv CHRIENG kaa-raa-ou-khei tei?
After the film, shall we sing karaoke?
You
ខ្ញុំច្រៀងមិនពីរោះទេ!
khnyom chrieng min PI-ROH tei!
I don’t sing well!
Friend
អត់អីទេ! សប្បាយជាងសំខាន់។
ot ei tei! SA-BAY chieng som-khan.
Never mind! Having fun matters more.
Say It Right

ច្រៀង (chrieng) is “to sing” and ពីរោះ (pi-roh) is “melodious”. The same word praises a singer and a foreigner’s Khmer.

Pro-Tip · Sing Badly, Sing Anyway

Karaoke in Cambodia is done in private rooms with friends and family rather than in front of a bar, and the point is participation, not talent. Refusing the microphone repeatedly is the only real mistake — sing one song, badly, and you will have made a dozen friends. Note that some venues advertised as “KTV” are hostess bars rather than family karaoke; if you are unsure, go where colleagues take you.

Sport & Football

កីឡា និងបាល់ទាត់

Football is the universal conversation. So is the local boxing on Sunday afternoons.

Friend
យប់នេះមានបាល់ទាត់។ មើលទេ?
yub nih mien BAL-toat. meul tei?
There’s football tonight. Watching?
You
មើល! អ្នកគាំទ្រក្រុមណា?
MEUL! neak koam-tro krom naa?
Yes! Which team do you support?
Friend
ខ្ញុំគាំទ្រក្រុមកម្ពុជា។
khnyom koam-TRO krom kam-pu-chie.
I support the Cambodian team.
You
ស្គរប៉ុន្មានហើយ?
SKO pon-man haoy?
What’s the score?
Friend
មួយសូន្យ។ ឈ្នះហើយ!
muoy SOUN. chhneah haoy!
One–nil. We’ve won!
Say It Right

គាំទ្រ (koam-tro) means “to support”, of a team or a person. ឈ្នះ (chhneah) is win; ចាញ់ (chanh) is lose.

Phrases

Pro-Tip · Kun Khmer, Not Muay Thai

Cambodia’s traditional kickboxing is គុនខ្មែរ (kun khmae), broadcast live on Sunday afternoons and followed passionately. Calling it Muay Thai will get you a firm correction — the question of which country originated the sport is a genuinely sensitive one. Football is the other national obsession, and an evening watching the Cambodian national team in a riverside café is one of the easiest ways into ordinary conversation.

Travel, Culture & Leisure

Speaking of History

ការនិយាយអំពីប្រវត្តិសាស្ត្រ

The hardest conversation in this book. Listen far more than you speak, and let the other person lead.

You
ខ្ញុំចង់រៀនប្រវត្តិសាស្ត្រកម្ពុជា។
khnyom chong rien bra-voat-te-SAAH kam-pu-chie.
I want to learn Cambodian history.
Friend
សម័យអង្គរ គឺជាសម័យរុងរឿង។
sa-may ANG-KO keu chie sa-may rung-roeung.
The Angkor period was a golden age.
You
ខ្ញុំបានទៅសារមន្ទីរតួលស្លែង។
khnyom baan teuv saa-ra-mon-TII Tuol Sleng.
I visited the Tuol Sleng museum.
Friend
គ្រួសារយើងជាច្រើនបានបាត់បង់។
kruo-saa yeung chie chraen baan BAT-bong.
Many of our families were lost.
You
ខ្ញុំសោកស្ដាយណាស់។ អរគុណដែលប្រាប់។
khnyom saok-SDAY nas. or-kun dael brab.
I’m very sorry. Thank you for telling me.
Say It Right

សោកស្ដាយ (saok-sday) means “to be sorry / to grieve” — sorrow, not apology. It is the right word when someone tells you of a loss.

Ngorn Kakteka188Prepared by Nat Bunchhai

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics

The Angkor periodសម័យអង្គរsa-may ang-ko
I want to learn about …ខ្ញុំចង់រៀនអំពី …khnyom chong rien om-pii …
Museumសារមន្ទីរsaa-ra-mon-tii
I’m very sorry. (for a loss)ខ្ញុំសោកស្ដាយណាស់khnyom saok-sday nas
Thank you for telling me.អរគុណដែលប្រាប់ខ្ញុំor-kun dael brab khnyom
Cambodia is at peace now.ឥឡូវកម្ពុជាមានសន្តិភាពeu-lov kam-pu-chie mien son-te-phiep

Pro-Tip · Let Them Raise It First

Almost every Cambodian family lost people under the Khmer Rouge, and almost everyone you meet is connected to that loss. It is not a topic to open over lunch out of curiosity. If someone chooses to tell you their family’s story, that is a considerable trust: listen, don’t compare, don’t ask for details, and thank them. Visit Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek quietly and without photographing yourself there. Cambodians are far more eager to talk about Angkor, about their food and about the future.

Post Office & Parcels

ប្រៃសណីយ៍ និងកញ្ចប់

Sending something home. Ask the price both ways — air and sea differ enormously.

You
ខ្ញុំចង់ផ្ញើកញ្ចប់ទៅបារាំង។
khnyom chong phnhaeu kon-CHOP teuv baa-rang.
I’d like to send a parcel to France.
Clerk
ផ្ញើតាមអាកាស ឬតាមសមុទ្រ?
phnhaeu taam aa-KAAH reu taam sa-mot?
By air or by sea?
You
តាមអាកាស។ ថ្លៃប៉ុន្មាន?
taam aa-KAAH. thlai pon-man?
By air. How much?
Clerk
សែសិបដុល្លារ ដល់ក្នុងពីរអាទិត្យ។
SAE-sep dol-laa, dol knong pii aa-tit.
Forty dollars, arriving in two weeks.
You
សុំលេខតាមដានផង។
som leik taam-DAAN phong.
A tracking number, please.
Say It Right

ផ្ញើ (phnhaeu) covers sending parcels, messages and money alike. តាមដាន (taam-daan) means “to track / follow”.

Post Office & Parcels

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics

It’s fragile.វាងាយបែកvie ngiey baek
Pro-Tip · Use a Courier for Anything Valuable

The state post is inexpensive but slow, and parcels are opened for customs inspection as a matter of routine. For documents or anything of value, use an international courier — more expensive, insured, and genuinely trackable. Never post cash. Note that incoming parcels frequently attract a customs charge on collection, and that the address to give senders is the post office box, since street delivery outside the main cities is limited.

Visa Extension

ការពន្យារទិដ្ឋាការ

At the immigration office. Bring the passport, the photos and more patience than you think you need.

You
ខ្ញុំចង់ពន្យារទិដ្ឋាការ។
khnyom chong pon-yie tet-thaa-KAA.
I’d like to extend my visa.
Officer
ពន្យារប៉ុន្មានខែ?
pon-yie pon-man KHAE?
For how many months?
You
មួយឆ្នាំ។ ត្រូវការឯកសារអ្វីខ្លះ?
muoy chhnam. trov-kaa aek-ka-SAA a-vei khlah?
One year. What documents do I need?
Officer
លិខិតឆ្លងដែន និងរូបថតពីរសន្លឹក។
li-khet chhlong-daen ning ruup-THOT pii son-leuk.
Passport and two photographs.
You
ពេលណាមកយកវិញ?
peil naa mok YOK vinh?
When do I collect it?
Say It Right

ពន្យារ (pon-yie) means “to extend / postpone” — the same verb for a visa, a deadline and a meeting.

Ngorn Kakteka193Prepared by Nat Bunchhai

92

Visa Extension

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
Visaទិដ្ឋាការtet-thaa-kaa
I’d like to extend my visa.ខ្ញុំចង់ពន្យារទិដ្ឋាការkhnyom chong pon-yie tet-thaa-kaa

Documentsឯកសារaek-ka-saa
Photographsរូបថតruup-thot
Work permitលិខិតអនុញ្ញាតការងារli-khet a-nu-nhat kaa-ngie
My visa has expired.ទិដ្ឋាការខ្ញុំផុតកំណត់tet-thaa-kaa khnyom phot kom-not
When can I collect it?ពេលណាមកយកវិញ?peil naa mok yok vinh?
Pro-Tip · Get the Right Visa on Arrival

The tourist visa (T) can be extended only once, for a month. The ordinary visa (E) is the one that extends for six months or a year and permits work — and you cannot switch from T to E without leaving the country. Ask for the E class at the airport if there is any chance you will stay. Overstaying is fined per day at the border and quickly becomes expensive; most long-term residents use an agent, which costs a little more and saves the queue entirely.

Barber & Hair Salon

ហាងកាត់សក់

A haircut costs a couple of dollars. Say how much to take off — and show a photo if you can.

You
សុំកាត់សក់។ ខ្លីបន្តិច។
som kat SOK. khlei bon-tech.
A haircut, please. A little short.
Barber
ខ្លីប៉ុណ្ណា? ខាងក្រោយវិញ?
KHLEI pon-naa? khang-kraoy vinh?
How short? And the back?
You
ខាងក្រោយខ្លី ខាងលើទុកវែង។
khang-kraoy KHLEI, khang-leu tuk veng.
Short at the back, leave the top long.
You
កុំកាត់ខ្លីពេក។
kom kat KHLEI peik.
Don’t cut it too short.
Barber
កោរពុកមាត់ផងទេ?
KAO puk-moat phong tei?
Shall I shave you as well?
Say It Right

ខ្លី (khlei) is short and វែង (veng) is long. Add peik — “too” — for the word every haircut needs: kom kat khlei peik.

Barber & Hair Salon

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
Haircutកាត់សក់kat sok
Short / longខ្លី / វែងkhlei / veng
Don’t cut it too short.កុំកាត់ខ្លីពេកkom kat khlei peik
Just a trim.កាត់តិចតួចkat tech-tuoch

Pro-Tip · Show a Picture

Hair vocabulary is where careful learners still come unstuck, and the consequences last a month. Show a photograph on your phone and use douch ruup nih — “like this picture”. A cut usually includes a hair wash, a head and shoulder massage and sometimes an ear cleaning, all for two or three dollars. If you would rather skip the ear cleaning, min bach tei, or-kun declines it politely.

Talking to Children

ការនិយាយជាមួយក្មេងៗ

Children will call out to you everywhere. A few words back and you will have made their day.

Child
ហេឡូ! ហេឡូ!
hei-LOU! hei-lou!
Hello! Hello!
You
សួស្តី! ប្អូនឈ្មោះអ្វី?
suor-sdei! P’OUN chhmuoh a-vei?
Hi! What’s your name?
Child
ខ្ញុំឈ្មោះស្រីនាង។ អាយុប្រាំបីឆ្នាំ។
khnyom chhmuoh Srey Neang. aa-yuk PRAM-bei chhnam.
I’m Srey Neang. I’m eight years old.
You
ប្អូនរៀនថ្នាក់ទីប៉ុន្មាន?
p’oun rien thnak ti PON-MAN?
What grade are you in?
You
ពូកែណាស់! រៀនឲ្យបានល្អណា។
pu-KAE nas! rien aoy baan la-or naa.
Very clever! Study well.
Say It Right

Call a child ប្អូន (p’oun) — “younger one”. They will call you bong, or om if you are their parents’ age or older.

Talking to Children

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
Child / childrenក្មេង / ក្មេងៗkmeng / kmeng-kmeng
What’s your name? (to a child)ប្អូនឈ្មោះអ្វី?p’oun chhmuoh a-vei?
How old are you?អាយុប៉ុន្មានឆ្នាំ?aa-yuk pon-man chhnam?
Do you go to school?ទៅសាលារៀនទេ?teuv saa-lie-rien tei?
Very clever!ពូកែណាស់!pu-kae nas!
Study hard.រៀនឲ្យបានល្អrien aoy baan la-or
Be careful!ប្រយ័ត្ន!bra-yat!
Where is your mother?ម្ដាយប្អូននៅឯណា?mdaay p’oun nov ae-naa?
Pro-Tip · Don’t Pat the Head

Ruffling a child’s hair is affectionate in the West and quietly wrong here: the head is the most sacred part of the body. A smile, a wave and a question about school are the right warmth. Please also do not hand money or sweets to begging children, however hard that is — it keeps them working the streets instead of at school. If you want to help, give to a school or a registered organisation instead.

Pets & the Vet

សត្វចិញ្ចឹម និងពេទ្យសត្វ

Taking a dog or cat to the clinic, and the words for the street dogs you will meet everywhere.

You
ឆ្កែខ្ញុំឈឺ មិនញ៉ាំអាហារ។
CHHKAE khnyom chheu, min nyam aa-haa.
My dog is sick, it isn’t eating.
Vet
ប៉ុន្មានថ្ងៃហើយ? អាយុប៉ុន្មាន?
pon-man thngai haoy? AA-YUK pon-man?
For how long? How old is it?
You
ពីរថ្ងៃ។ អាយុបីឆ្នាំ។
PII thngai. aa-yuk bei chhnam.
Two days. It’s three years old.
Vet
ត្រូវចាក់វ៉ាក់សាំងផងទេ?
trov chak VAK-sang phong tei?
Does it need vaccinations as well?
You
បាទ ចាក់ថ្នាំកំចាត់ឆ្កួតជ្រូកផង។
baat, chak thnam kom-chat CHHKUOT phong.
Yes, the rabies vaccination too.
Say It Right

ឆ្កែ (chhkae) is dog and ឆ្មា (chhmaa) is cat. Both begin with the breathy chh that also starts chheu, to hurt.

Ngorn Kakteka199Prepared by Nat Bunchhai
Chapter 10 · Daily Life & AdminSituation 95

Pets & the Vet

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics

Vetពេទ្យសត្វpeit sat

Pro-Tip · Rabies Is Real Here

Cambodia has one of the world’s highest rates of rabies deaths, and street dogs are everywhere. Do not approach or feed them, and if you are bitten or even scratched, wash the wound with soap for fifteen minutes and get to a clinic the same day — the Institut Pasteur in Phnom Penh provides the vaccine. Pre-exposure vaccination is well worth it for anyone living here, especially cyclists and families with children.

Traffic, Noise & Grumbles

ចរាចរណ៍ សំឡេង និងការត្អូញត្អែរ

The daily complaints of city life. Shared grumbling is a genuine social glue — join in.

Friend
ថ្ងៃនេះស្ទះចរាចរណ៍ខ្លាំងណាស់។
thngai nih STOAH cha-raa-chor khlang nas.
The traffic is terrible today.
You
មែនហើយ! ខ្ញុំមកយឺតកន្លះម៉ោង។
maen haoy! khnyom mok YOEUT kon-lah maong.
Yes! I was half an hour late.
You
យប់មិញសំឡេងខ្លាំងណាស់។
yub minh SOM-LENG khlang nas.
Last night was so noisy.
Friend
មានពិធីមង្គលការជិតផ្ទះ។
mien pi-thii mong-kol-KAA chit phteah.
There’s a wedding near the house.
You
ធូលីច្រើនណាស់ក្នុងរដូវប្រាំង។
thou-LII chraen nas knong ro-dov prang.
So much dust in the dry season.
Say It Right

ស្ទះ (stoah) means “blocked” — of traffic, a drain or a nose alike. stoah cha-raa-chor is a traffic jam.

Traffic, Noise & Grumbles

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
Traffic jamស្ទះចរាចរណ៍stoah cha-raa-chor
I was late.ខ្ញុំមកយឺតkhnyom mok yoeut
It’s very noisy.សំឡេងខ្លាំងណាស់som-leng khlang nas
Dustធូលីthou-lii
The road is flooded.ផ្លូវលិចទឹកphlov lech tuk
Be careful on the road.ប្រយ័ត្នពេលបើកបរbra-yat peil baeuk-bor
It’s always like this.តែងតែបែបនេះtaeng-tae baep nih
Never mind, that’s life.អត់អីទេ ជីវិតបែបនេះot ei tei, chi-vit baep nih
Pro-Tip · Grumble Sideways, Not Upward

Complaining companionably about heat, traffic and dust is friendly and expected; complaining at a person about their service or their country is not, and lands much harder than you intend. Note the useful national shrug: អត់អីទេ (ot ei tei) — “never mind”. It carries a genuine Buddhist patience with things that cannot be changed, and reaching for it instead of frustration will make your life here considerably easier.

Opinions & Disagreeing

មតិ និងការមិនយល់ស្រប

Saying what you think, and differing without confrontation. The softening words are the skill here.

Friend
អ្នកគិតយ៉ាងម៉េចដែរ?
neak ket yang MECH dae?
What do you think?
You
ខ្ញុំគិតថាវាល្អ។
khnyom KET thaa vie la-or.
I think it’s good.
Friend
ខ្ញុំមិនសូវយល់ស្របទេ។
khnyom min sao yul-SROP tei.
I don’t quite agree.
You
អ្នកនិយាយត្រូវដែរ។
neak ni-yiey TROV dae.
You have a point too.
You
តាមខ្ញុំគិត ប្រហែលបែបនេះល្អជាង។
taam khnyom ket, bra-hael BAEP nih la-or chieng.
In my view, perhaps this way is better.
Say It Right

មិនសូវ (min sao) means “not very / not quite” and is the great softener. min sao yul-srop is a firm disagreement wearing good manners.

Ngorn Kakteka203Prepared by Nat Bunchhai
Chapter 10 · Daily Life & AdminSituation 97
97

Opinions & Disagreeing

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
What do you think?អ្នកគិតយ៉ាងម៉េចដែរ?neak ket yang mech dae?
I think that …ខ្ញុំគិតថា …khnyom ket thaa …
In my viewតាមខ្ញុំគិតtaam khnyom ket
I agree.ខ្ញុំយល់ស្របkhnyom yul-srop
I don’t quite agree.ខ្ញុំមិនសូវយល់ស្របទេkhnyom min sao yul-srop tei
You have a point.អ្នកនិយាយត្រូវដែរneak ni-yiey trov dae
Maybe / perhapsប្រហែលbra-hael
It depends.អាស្រ័យaa-srey
Pro-Tip · Avoid Politics With Strangers

Cambodians discuss food, family, football and money freely, and national politics far more carefully — particularly with a foreigner they have just met. If a political conversation starts, listen and ask questions rather than offering verdicts about a country you are a guest in. The same applies to religion. Aa-srey, “it depends”, and bra-hael, “perhaps”, are perfectly respectable places to leave an opinion.

Telling a Story

ការនិទានរឿង

Khmer verbs never change form. Past, present and future are handled by three little words.

Friend
ម្សិលមិញអ្នកទៅណា?
msel-minh neak TEUV naa?
Where did you go yesterday?
You
ខ្ញុំបានទៅសៀមរាប។
khnyom BAAN teuv siem-riep.
I went to Siem Reap.
You
កាលពីម្សិលមិញភ្លៀងធ្លាក់ខ្លាំង។
kaal-pii msel-minh PLEANG thleak khlang.
Yesterday it rained heavily.
You
ឥឡូវខ្ញុំកំពុងសម្រាក។
eu-lov khnyom KOM-PUNG som-raak.
Right now I’m resting.
You
ថ្ងៃស្អែកខ្ញុំនឹងទៅធ្វើការ។
thngai sa-aek khnyom NEUNG teuv thveu kaa.
Tomorrow I will go to work.
Say It Right

Three markers carry all of Khmer tense: បាន (baan) before a verb for the past, កំពុង (kom-pung) for right now, នឹង (neung) for the future.

98

Telling a Story

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
Past marker (before the verb)បានbaan
Happening nowកំពុងkom-pung
Future markerនឹងneung
Yesterday / today / tomorrowម្សិលមិញ / ថ្ងៃនេះ / ថ្ងៃស្អែកmsel-minh / thngai nih / thngai sa-aek
Last week / next weekអាទិត្យមុន / អាទិត្យក្រោយaa-tit mun / aa-tit kraoy
Then / after thatបន្ទាប់មកbon-toab mok
Suddenlyភ្លាមៗphliem-phliem
Really? / is that so?មែនអ៊ីចឹង?maen ei-cheung?
Pro-Tip · The Time Word Does the Work

Because verbs never conjugate, Khmer usually drops the tense marker altogether once a time word has been said: msel-minh khnyom teuv … — “yesterday I go” — is complete and natural. Put the time word at the front of the sentence and the rest looks after itself. This is the moment most learners realise Khmer grammar is far kinder than its script suggests.

Daily Life & Admin

Requests & Favours

ការស្នើសុំ និងជំនួយ

Asking for help, and offering it. One structure — chuoy … phong — does almost all of it.

You
សុំរំខានបន្តិច។ ជួយខ្ញុំបានទេ?
som rom-KHAN bon-tech. chuoy khnyom baan tei?
Sorry to bother you. Could you help me?
Friend
បាន! មានរឿងអ្វី?
BAAN! mien roeung a-vei?
Sure! What is it?
You
ជួយបកប្រែឲ្យខ្ញុំបន្តិចផង។
chuoy bok-BRAE aoy khnyom bon-tech phong.
Please translate this for me.
Friend
អត់បញ្ហាទេ។
ot bon-HAA tei.
No problem at all.
You
អរគុណណាស់ អ្នកជួយខ្ញុំច្រើន។
or-kun nas, neak CHUOY khnyom chraen.
Thank you, you’ve helped me a lot.
Say It Right

The polite request frame is chuoy + verb + phong. សុំរំខានបន្តិច (som rom-khan bon-tech) — “sorry to disturb” — is the perfect opener.

Requests & Favours

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
Sorry to bother you.សុំរំខានបន្តិចsom rom-khan bon-tech
Could you help me?ជួយខ្ញុំបានទេ?chuoy khnyom baan tei?
Please translate for me.ជួយបកប្រែឲ្យខ្ញុំផងchuoy bok-brae aoy khnyom phong
Could you lend me …?ខ្ចី … បានទេ?khchei … baan tei?
No problem at all.អត់បញ្ហាទេot bon-haa tei
Can I help you?ខ្ញុំជួយអ្នកបានទេ?khnyom chuoy neak baan tei?
You’ve helped me a lot.អ្នកជួយខ្ញុំច្រើនneak chuoy khnyom chraen
I owe you one.ខ្ញុំជំពាក់គុណអ្នកkhnyom chum-peak kun neak
Pro-Tip · Favours Are a Ledger, Not a Transaction

Help given here creates a warm, unspoken obligation that runs in both directions and is never settled with cash. If a colleague spends their Saturday helping you deal with a landlord, the way to repay it is to be available when their family needs something — not to hand them money, which turns a friendship into a service. The word for this debt of kindness is គុណ (kun), and it also sits inside or-kun, thank you.

Ngorn Kakteka208Prepared by Nat Bunchhai

Daily Life & Admin

Farewells & Blessings

ការលា និងការជូនពរ

The last page. Leaving well matters as much as arriving well — and takes longer than you expect.

You
ខ្ញុំនឹងត្រឡប់ទៅស្រុកខ្ញុំវិញ។
khnyom neung tro-lop teuv SROK khnyom vinh.
I’m going back to my country.
Friend
យើងនឹងនឹករលឹកអ្នកណាស់។
yeung neung NEUK ro-leuk neak nas.
We will miss you very much.
You
អរគុណសម្រាប់អ្វីៗទាំងអស់។
or-kun som-rap a-vei-vei TEANG-oh.
Thank you for everything.
Friend
សូមធ្វើដំណើរដោយសុវត្ថិភាព។
som thveu dom-naeu daoy so-vat-thi-PHIEP.
Have a safe journey.
You
ខ្ញុំនឹងត្រឡប់មកវិញ។ ជម្រាបលា។
khnyom neung tro-lop MOK vinh. chom-riep lie.
I’ll come back. Goodbye.
Say It Right

ជម្រាបលា (chom-riep lie) is the formal farewell, the mirror of chom-riep suor on page one. You have come full circle.

Ngorn Kakteka209Prepared by Nat Bunchhai

Farewells & Blessings

Phrases

Key Phrases

EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
Goodbye (formal)ជម្រាបលាchom-riep lie
Have a safe journey.សូមធ្វើដំណើរដោយសុវត្ថិភាពsom thveu dom-naeu daoy so-vat-thi-phiep
Good luck!សូមឲ្យមានសំណាងល្អ!som aoy mien som-nang la-or!
Take care of your health.ថែរក្សាសុខភាពផងthae-rak-saa sok-kha-phiep phong
We will miss you.យើងនឹងនឹករលឹកអ្នកyeung neung neuk ro-leuk neak
Thank you for everything.អរគុណសម្រាប់អ្វីៗទាំងអស់or-kun som-rap a-vei-vei teang-oh
I’ll come back.ខ្ញុំនឹងត្រឡប់មកវិញkhnyom neung tro-lop mok vinh
May you be happy and well.សូមឲ្យមានសុខភាពល្អsom aoy mien sok-kha-phiep la-or
Pro-Tip · Goodbyes Take an Hour

Leaving a Cambodian gathering is not a single act but a slow circuit: you announce your departure, are pressed to stay, eat a little more, announce it again, and are walked all the way to your motorbike. Allow for it — leaving abruptly is the one discourtesy. And when you do finally go, the blessing you give matters more than the farewell itself. Som aoy mien sok-kha-phiep la-or — may you have good health — is never the wrong thing to say.

About This Book

អំពីសៀវភៅនេះ

This book was built backwards from the way people actually learn a language in Cambodia: by being dropped into a moment they cannot avoid, and needing eight words to get through it. Each of the hundred situations was chosen because it happens — at a coffee stall, a pharmacy counter, a landlord’s doorway, a wedding — not because it fits a grammar syllabus. The grammar is still there. It arrives quietly, underneath the phrases, once the mouth has already moved.

Wrote the hundred situations, the dialogues and every cultural note in this volume — the accumulated answer to a decade of the same questions from newcomers who wanted to stop pointing and start speaking.

ណ

Nat Bunchhai

One Last Pro-Tip

Do not wait until you are ready. Cambodians forgive a foreigner’s grammar instantly and remember the attempt for years. Say the wrong thing warmly, today. សូមសំណាងល្អ! (som som-nang la-or!)

Teacher’s GuideBefore you begin

How to Teach With This Deck

របៀបប្រើមេរៀននេះក្នុងថ្នាក់
1

Every situation runs on the same five slides ≈ 12 min

Opener → Dialogue → Key Phrases → Pro-Tip → Practice. Students always know what comes next, so the cognitive load goes into the language, not the format.

2

Model twice, then drill

Read each Khmer line at natural speed, then broken into syllables. Class repeats chorally, then in halves, then individually. Never explain grammar before the mouth has moved.

3

Press R to hide the English column

The Khmer and the phonetics stay on screen while the meaning disappears — students must produce the English, or better, act the phrase out. Press R again to check.

4

Finish standing up

The Practice slide is always pair work performed on their feet. A situation is not “taught” until every student has said it aloud to another human being.

Situation 01 · Saying Hello & GoodbyeCulture

The Sampeah

សំពះ
How high do the hands go?

Chest — friends and peers.
Mouth — elders, teachers, bosses.
Nose bridge — monks, officials, the king.

Returning a sampeah correctly is the single gesture Cambodians remember a foreigner for.

Baat or Chaa?

Men end polite sentences with បាទ (baat). Women use ចាស (chaa).

It marks the speaker’s own gender, never the listener’s — the mistake almost every beginner makes in week one.

Ngorn Kakteka · prepared by Nat Bunchhai
Situation 01 · Saying Hello & GoodbyePractice

Practice 6 min

1

Chorus drill 2 min

Teacher says each line, class repeats. Then split the room: left side is the Owner, right side is You. Swap. Speed up on the third pass.

2

Mingle 3 min

Everyone stands and greets five different classmates, using the sampeah and the correct particle. Full exchange each time: greet → ask → answer → leave.

3

Cold call 1 min

Press R, point at the Khmer, and ask three students what it means. Anyone who answers in English must then say it in Khmer.

Homework

Greet one real Cambodian outside class today — a guard, a seller, a driver — and report tomorrow what they said back.

សុខទុក្ខ និងការសួរនាំ
By the end of this situation students can report how they feel — well, tired, busy, unwell — bounce the question back, and handle Cambodia’s real greeting: “Have you eaten yet?”

Meeting a neighbour you haven’t seen in weeks
Neighbour
អូ! យូរហើយមិនបានជួបគ្នា។
ouh! YOO haoy min baan chuop knie.

Neighbour
ធម្មតាទេ តែរវល់ណាស់។ ចុះបងវិញ?
thoam-ma-DAA tei, tae ro-VOL nas. choh bong vinh?

Neighbour
ញ៉ាំបាយហើយនៅ?

ញ៉ាំហើយ បាទ។ អរគុណ។
NYAM haoy, baat. or-kun.

Ngorn Kakteka · prepared by Nat Bunchhai
Situation 02 · How Are You?Culture

“Have You Eaten Yet?”

ញ៉ាំបាយហើយនៅ?
Not a question about food

This is Cambodia’s everyday “How’s it going?” — rooted in generations for whom a full stomach was the truest measure that life was going well.

Answer nyam haoy (ញ៉ាំហើយ, “already eaten”) unless you actually want lunch. Saying nov tei (នៅទេ, “not yet”) is very often heard as accepting an invitation you did not know you had received.

Say it right · the question tag

The tag …ទេ? (tei?) turns any statement into a yes/no question — and it barely rises. Khmer does not swing pitch the way English does; over-lifting the ending sounds anxious rather than friendly.

Ngorn Kakteka · prepared by Nat Bunchhai
Situation 02 · How Are You?Practice

Practice 6 min

1

Feelings line-up 2 min

Give each student a secret mood — sok sa-bay, nuey-hot, ro-vol, min sao sruol kluon. They must answer in character; the class guesses.

2

The bounce-back drill 2 min

Nobody may answer without returning ចុះអ្នកវិញ? (choh neak vinh?). Run it around the whole room without a pause.

3

Trap the class 2 min

Ask ញ៉ាំបាយហើយនៅ? at speed. Anyone who answers nov tei has just accepted your invitation — and owes the room a sentence in Khmer about what they will eat.

Ngorn Kakteka · prepared by Nat Bunchhai

Situation 03 · Introducing YourselfCulture

Age Decides the Pronoun

ការប្រើសព្វនាមតាមអាយុ
There is no neutral “you”

បង bong — slightly older
ប្អូន p’oun — younger
លោក / លោកស្រី lowk / lowk srei — formal, senior
ឪម om — your parents’ generation

The safe default

Calling an older person bong is always safe. Calling them p’oun is not.

Expect the family name first: the author of this course, Ngorn Kakteka, is addressed as Kakteka.

Ngorn Kakteka · prepared by Nat Bunchhai
Situation 03 · Introducing YourselfPractice

Practice 7 min

1

Build your own line 2 min

Each student writes their four sentences: name, country, job, Khmer level. Teacher circulates and corrects pronunciation only — not grammar.

2

Speed introductions 3 min

Two rows facing each other. Thirty seconds per pair, then one row shifts left. Every student introduces themselves at least six times.

3

Pronoun test 2 min

Teacher names a person — “the market seller, about 60” — and the class calls out the correct pronoun. Anyone who says p’oun to an elder starts again.

Next class

Situations 04–06: Asking Someone’s Name · Please, Thank You & Sorry · Yes, No & “I Don’t Understand”.

Situation 04 · Asking Someone’s NameCulture
Pro-Tip · Everyone Has Two Names

The name on the ID card is often not the name anyone uses. Most Cambodians go by a one-syllable nickname given in childhood — Ti, Srey, Bong, Nak — and colleagues of twenty years may never learn the formal one. Ask for the ឈ្មោះហៅក្រៅ (chhmuoh hav krav) and use it. Attach bong or p’oun in front and you sound like a local, not a form.

Say it right

ភ្លេច (phlech) starts with a puffed p, not an f. English speakers reach for “flech” — the mouth position is closer to “p-lech” said quickly.

Ngorn Kakteka · prepared by Nat Bunchhai

Situation 05 · Please, Thank You & SorryKey Phrases
EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
Please … (before a verb)សូម …som …
Thank youអរគុណor-kun

Situation 05 · Please, Thank You & SorryCulture
Pro-Tip · There Is No “You’re Welcome”

Khmer has no single reply to thanks. Cambodians answer with អត់អីទេ (ot ei tei) or មិនអីទេ (min ei tei) — both meaning “it’s nothing”. And សូមទោស does double duty: it is your apology and your “excuse me” for squeezing past someone in a crowded market. Say it with a small dip of the head and it never sounds abrupt.

Say it right

សូម (som) rhymes with English “some” and goes in front of the verb, never at the end: som brab, not “brab som”.

Ngorn Kakteka · prepared by Nat Bunchhai

Someone is speaking to you at full speed. These five sentences buy you time without ending the conversation.

Situation 06 · Yes, No & “I Don’t Understand”Key Phrases
EnglishKhmer ScriptRomanized Phonetics
Yes (male / female)បាទ / ចាសbaat / chaa
No / notទេ / អត់ទេtei / ot tei

I don’t understand.ខ្ញុំមិនយល់ទេkhnyom min yul tei

Ngorn Kakteka · prepared by Nat Bunchhai
Situation 06 · Yes, No & “I Don’t Understand”Culture
Pro-Tip · “Yes” Often Means “I’m Listening”

A Cambodian nodding baat, baat, baat through your explanation is telling you they can hear you — not that they agree, and not that they understood. Direct refusal is felt as harsh, so a genuine “no” usually arrives dressed as “maybe”, “a bit difficult”, or a smile and silence. When something matters, ask the person to tell you the plan back in their own words.

Say it right

The negative is a sandwich: min … tei wraps around the verb. ខ្ញុំមិនយល់ទេ is literally “I not understand no”. Drop the final tei and it sounds unfinished.

Ngorn Kakteka · prepared by Nat Bunchhai

Situation 07 · Repeat & Speak SlowlyCulture
Pro-Tip · Ask for the Pen

Cambodian numbers are the hardest thing on this page to hear at speed, and every price in the country is negotiable in writing. Carrying a small notebook — or handing over your phone’s calculator — turns a failed exchange into a friendly one in two seconds. Sellers do this with each other constantly; it is not a foreigner’s crutch, it is normal practice.

Say it right

Doubling a word softens or stretches it. យឺតៗ (yoeut-yoeut) is “slowly, slowly”; the little mark ៗ means “say it twice”. You will see it everywhere.

Ngorn Kakteka · prepared by Nat Bunchhai

Situation 08 · Where Are You From?Culture
Pro-Tip · The Questions That Follow

Expect the next three questions to be your age, marital status and salary — in that order, from someone you met four minutes ago. This is not nosiness. Age settles which pronoun to use, and the rest is ordinary friendly accounting. A vague answer is perfectly acceptable: ចាំមួយភ្លែត (cham muoy phlet — “hang on a second”) and a laugh closes the subject with no offence taken.

Say it right

The country’s own name is កម្ពុជា (kam-pu-chie) — four beats, stress light throughout. “Cambodia” is the English exonym; using the Khmer one always earns a smile.

Ngorn Kakteka · prepared by Nat Bunchhai

Cambodia has two seasons and one universal complaint. Both are excellent conversation starters.

Situation 09 · Talking About the WeatherCulture
Pro-Tip · Complaining Is Bonding

Grumbling about the heat is a social ritual, not a conversation about meteorology. A well-timed ក្ដៅណាស់! to a stranger waiting out a downpour with you will get a laugh and often a chair. Note also that Cambodians divide the year into hot, rainy and a brief, treasured cool season around December — mention preferring the cool one and you will get instant agreement.

Say it right

ក្ដៅ (kdav) is one syllable — the k and d are pressed together with no vowel between them. Khmer is full of these clusters; resist the urge to insert “kuh-dav”.

Ngorn Kakteka · prepared by Nat Bunchhai

Situation 10 · Numbers & Telling TimeCulture
Pro-Tip · Read the Price Tags

Khmer has its own numerals — ១ ២ ៣ ៤ ៥ ៦ ៧ ៨ ៩ ០ — and they appear on market price tags, bus tickets, house numbers and government forms, often instead of Western digits. Ten minutes spent memorising the shapes will save you a hundred confused transactions. Note that ៥ (5) and ៨ (8) are the two most commonly misread by beginners.

Say it right

Khmer counts to five, then adds: six is pram-muoy (5+1), seven pram-pil (5+2), up to nine. Hear pram- and you already know the number is between six and nine.

Situation 11 · Hailing a Tuk-TukCulture
Pro-Tip · Tuk-Tuk, Remork, Moto

What tourists call a tuk-tuk, Cambodians usually call a រ៉ឺម៉ក (rermok) — a carriage towed behind a motorbike. The small Indian-style auto-rickshaws that arrived with the ride apps are the true tuk-tuk, and they are cheaper. A moto-dup — you riding pillion on a motorbike — is cheapest and fastest of all, and is how most of Phnom Penh actually moves.

Say it right

Settle the price before you climb in — cham bon-tech (“hold on a second”) is the phrase that buys you that moment, and every Cambodian passenger uses it.

Situation 12 · Negotiating the FareCulture
Pro-Tip · The Round-Trip Discount

The strongest card you hold is not haggling — it is volume. Asking a driver to wait and bring you back (teuv mok vinh phong) often costs barely more than the one-way fare, because he keeps the fare instead of hunting a new passenger. Do this twice with the same driver and you have a regular: save his number, and you will never negotiate again.

Say it right

ថ្លៃ (thlai) means expensive; តម្លៃ (tom-lai) means price. One syllable apart, and mixing them up is the most common bargaining slip.

Ngorn Kakteka · prepared by Nat Bunchhai

Situation 13 · Directing the DriverCulture
Pro-Tip · Navigate by Landmark

Street numbers exist in Phnom Penh but almost nobody navigates by them, and outside the capital they barely exist at all. Cambodians steer by landmarks: វត្ត (voat, pagoda), ផ្សារ (phsaa, market), a petrol station, a well-known hotel. Learn the three landmarks nearest your home and you will never be lost again — “behind the pagoda” beats any address.

Say it right

ឆ្វេង (chveng, left) and ស្ដាំ (sdam, right) are worth over-learning. Point with your whole hand as you say them — pointing with one finger is impolite here.

Ngorn Kakteka · prepared by Nat Bunchhai

Situation 14 · Using a Ride AppCulture
Pro-Tip · The App Price Is the Real Price

Apps such as PassApp, Grab and TADA fix the fare in advance, which quietly ends the whole negotiation game — and they are usually cheaper than a street tuk-tuk for a foreigner. Keep your phone in Khmer-friendly mode: drivers will phone rather than message, and they will speak fast. The four phrases above cover ninety per cent of those calls.

Say it right

On the phone, lead with where you are standing, not your name. khnyom nov muk … (“I’m in front of …”) is the single most useful sentence in this whole situation.

Situation 15 · Renting a MotorbikeCulture
Pro-Tip · Never Leave Your Passport

Many rental shops ask for your passport as security. Offer a photocopy plus a deposit instead — reputable shops accept this, and recovering a held passport during a dispute is genuinely difficult. Photograph the bike from all four sides before you ride off, scratches included, and check that the shop provides a helmet: police fine riders without one, and foreigners are stopped far more often.

Say it right

ជួល (chuol) covers both rent and hire. Say chuol muoy khae — “rent one month” — and the daily rate usually drops by half.

Situation 16 · At the Bus StationCulture
Pro-Tip · Buy the Day Before

Popular routes — Phnom Penh to Siem Reap, Sihanoukville, Battambang — sell out on weekends and vanish entirely around Khmer New Year and Pchum Ben, when the whole country travels home at once. Buy a day ahead, arrive thirty minutes early, and keep your ticket visible: seats are assigned but rarely enforced, and the polite passenger who shows up last stands.

Say it right

ចេញ (chenh) means to leave / depart and ដល់ (dol) means to arrive. Two words that answer nearly every travel question you will ever ask.

Situation 17 · On a Long-Distance BusCulture
Pro-Tip · The Assistant Runs the Bus

Every intercity bus has a young assistant who loads luggage, collects tickets and shouts the stops. He is the person to ask, not the driver. Learn his job title — ជំនួយការ (chum-nuoy-kaa) — or simply catch his eye with bong. Tell him your destination when you board and he will make sure you are off the bus at the right place.

Say it right

សូមប្រាប់ខ្ញុំពេលដល់ (som brab khnyom peil dol) — “tell me when we arrive” — is worth memorising whole. Say it to the driver’s assistant, not the driver, and you will be woken at the right town.

Situation 18 · Ferries & BoatsCulture
Pro-Tip · Ask About the Last Boat First

Island and river services run to the weather and the number of passengers, not to the timetable painted on the jetty. Before you board anything, ask touk chong-kraoy tro-lop maong pon-man? — “what time is the last boat back?” — and then take the one before it. In the rainy season a cancelled afternoon crossing can strand you overnight, and the guesthouses know it.

Say it right

ជិះ (chih) is the verb for riding anything you sit on — boat, bus, bike, horse, elephant. chih touk, chih moto, chih laan.

Situation 19 · Airport & ImmigrationCulture
Pro-Tip · Have the Exact Fee Ready

Visa-on-arrival is paid in US dollars, in cash, and the counter rarely gives change gracefully. Bring the exact amount plus a passport photo, and keep small notes separate from large ones. If anyone at the airport asks for an extra “processing fee” beyond the posted price, a calm som toh, khnyom min yul tei — “sorry, I don’t understand” — with a smile is remarkably effective.

Say it right

ស្នាក់នៅ (snak-nov) means to stay / lodge, as opposed to រស់នៅ (ruoh-nov), to live. Officials care a great deal about which one you say.

Situation 20 · Asking for DirectionsCulture
Pro-Tip · Nobody Will Tell You They Don’t Know

Saying “I don’t know” to a guest feels unhelpful, so a person who is unsure will often point anyway — confidently, and sometimes wrongly. The fix is simple: ask two people, a hundred metres apart, and go with the answer they agree on. Better still, show the place on your phone map; a picture removes the pressure to guess entirely.

Say it right

Open with សូមទោស (som toh) every single time. Walking up and launching straight into a question reads as abrupt, even when your Khmer is otherwise perfect.

Ngorn Kakteka · prepared by Nat Bunchhai

Situation 21 · Getting a TableCulture
Pro-Tip · Nobody Seats You

In most Cambodian restaurants there is no host at the door. You walk in, find a table and sit down; staff arrive once you are settled. To call a waiter, raise a hand and say bong! — it is normal, not rude. What is rude is clicking your fingers or calling out “hey”. And the plastic-stool place with no menu is often the best food on the street.

Say it right

People are counted with នាក់ (neak): pii neak, bei neak. Say the number first, then the counter — never the other way round.

Ngorn Kakteka · prepared by Nat Bunchhai

Situation 22 · Ordering FoodCulture
Pro-Tip · Order the Way Cambodians Do

A Khmer meal is shared: two or three dishes land in the middle with a communal bowl of rice, and everybody takes small amounts onto their own plate. Ordering one dish each, Western style, produces a strange table. Ask muk naa chhngañ? — “which dish is delicious?” — and let the waiter build the meal. You will eat better and spend less.

Say it right

Quantity goes last: som bay-chhaa muoy is “please, fried rice, one”. Front-loading the number the English way — “one fried rice” — is understood, but marks you instantly.

Situation 23 · Drinks & CoffeeCulture
Pro-Tip · Sweet Is the Default

Cambodian coffee arrives with a thick layer of condensed milk at the bottom and sugar on top of that. If you want it plain, say so before the glass is built — afterwards nothing can be done. Ask for កាហ្វេខ្មៅ (kaa-fei khmav), “black coffee”, and add kom dak sko. Ice in reputable shops is factory-made and safe; the cylindrical kind with a hole through the middle is the one to trust.

Say it right

កុំ (kom) is “don’t” and goes before the verb: kom dak sko — “don’t put sugar”. It is direct without being rude, which is exactly what you want when ordering.

Ngorn Kakteka · prepared by Nat Bunchhai
